name: Rameswara Swamy Temple
story: Ancient temple dedicated to Lord Shiva as Rameswara, believed to have been installed by Lord Rama.
highlight: The towering gopuram and intricate carvings.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: A significant pilgrimage site in West Godavari.

name: Sangameshwara Temple
story: Part of the Navabrahma temple group at the confluence of the Tungabhadra and Krishna rivers, this 7th-century temple is a Chalukyan gem.
highlight: The exquisite Chalukyan stone carvings and river-confluence setting.

moreDetails.history: Built in the 7th century by the Badami Chalukyas, part of the Navabrahma temple complex.
moreDetails.architecture: Early Chalukyan Nagara style with finely carved temple walls.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Alampur is near the Srisailam dam backwaters.

name: Amareswara Swamy Temple (Amararama)
story: Situated on the banks of the Krishna River, this Pancharama Kshetra is believed to have a self-growing Shiva linga installed by Lord Indra.
highlight: The towering white marble linga and riverside setting.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Near the famous Amaravathi Buddhist stupa.

moreDetails.history: An ancient Pancharama Kshetra with a 15-foot marble linga said to be growing over time.
moreDetails.architecture: Dravidian temple with a large gopuram on the Krishna riverbank.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Amaravathi is also a major Buddhist heritage site.

name: Bhairavakona Cave Temple
story: A dramatic rock-cut cave shrine in the Nallamala Hills, often called nature's own Shiva temple.
highlight: The natural cave setting amid dense forests and waterfalls.
timings: Open daily; best visited during daylight.
entryNotes: Involves a forest trek; carry water and provisions.

moreDetails.history: 7th-8th century rock-cut caves in the Nallamala Hills.
moreDetails.architecture: Natural rock-cut cave shrines with carved panels.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: The waterfall near the caves is a scenic attraction.

name: Neelakantheswara Swamy Temple
story: Located near the Lakshmi Narasimha temple at the confluence of the Godavari and Bay of Bengal.
highlight: The proximity to the sea and river confluence (Sangam).
entryNotes: Usually visited along with the famous Narasimha temple.

moreDetails.history: Ancient temple at a sacred confluence point.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Take a boat ride to the exact point where river meets sea.

name: Someswara Swamy Temple
story: A coastal temple believed to have been installed by Sage Kapila, situated right on the beach.
highlight: The temple's location on the beach rocks.

moreDetails.history: Ancient temple with inscriptions dating to 12th century Cholas.
moreDetails.architecture: Simple stone structure on the coast.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: A scenic spot merging spirituality and sea views.

name: Shiva Temple
story: The main Shiva temple in Badvel, attracting devotees from the surrounding agricultural belt.

name: Omkareswara Swamy Temple
story: A sacred Shiva temple in Bandi Atmakur known for its ancient sanctity and association with the sacred syllable Om.
highlight: The spiritual significance of the Om-named temple.
entryNotes: In Nandyal district; plan combined trip with nearby temples.

moreDetails.history: An ancient Shiva temple in the Nandyal region.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Can be combined with visits to Mahanandi and other Nava Nandi temples.

name: Someswara Swamy Temple
story: A historic Shiva temple in the ancient coastal town of Bheemunipatnam, one of the oldest municipalities in India.
highlight: The coastal setting in one of India's oldest port towns.
entryNotes: Bheemunipatnam is a scenic beach town near Vizag.

moreDetails.history: Historic temple in one of the oldest municipalities and port towns of India.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Combine with a visit to Bheemunipatnam beach and Dutch cemetery.

name: Someswara Swamy Temple (Somarama)
story: The fifth Pancharama Kshetra, famous for its Shiva linga that is believed to change color with the phases of the moon.
highlight: The color-changing Shiva linga and the sacred Chandra Kundam pond.
entryNotes: Observe the linga's color on Pournami and Amavasya.

moreDetails.history: Ancient Pancharama Kshetra known for the lunar color-changing linga phenomenon.
moreDetails.architecture: Dravidian temple with the sacred Chandra Kundam tank.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Bhimavaram is a major town in West Godavari, well connected by rail.

name: Golingeswara Swamy Temple
story: A magnificent Eastern Chalukyan temple famous for its monolithic Nandi and rich sculptural heritage.
highlight: The exquisite Chalukyan stone carvings and the large Nandi.

moreDetails.history: Built by the Eastern Chalukyas (9th-10th century).
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Biccavolu has several other temples including a Ganesha temple.

name: Borra Guhalu Shiva Temple
story: Deep inside the million-year-old Borra Caves, a natural stalagmite formation is worshipped as a Shiva Linga.
highlight: The natural Shiva Linga formation inside the spectacular cave.

moreDetails.history: Natural cave formations dating back a million years.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: A major tourist attraction near Araku.

name: Kasi Visweswara Swamy Temple
story: Known as the Kasi of the South, famous for the water stream (Bugga) in the temple premise.
highlight: The perennial water source and serene surroundings.

moreDetails.history: Ancient temple held in high regard locally.

name: Sri Kapoteswara Swamy Temple
story: Associated with the legend of King Shibi who offered his own flesh to save a pigeon, the linga here is named after the kapota (pigeon).
highlight: The mythological connection to King Shibi's sacrifice.

moreDetails.history: Ancient temple linked to the Puranic legend of King Shibi and the pigeon.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: A pilgrimage site for those following the Shibi Chakravarthy legend.

name: Agastyeswara Swamy Temple
story: Another temple associated with Sage Agastya, featuring beautiful Chola architecture.
highlight: The Chola artistic influence and peaceful setting.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: A hidden gem for heritage lovers.

name: Pushpagiri Vaidyanatheswara Temple
story: Part of the ancient Pushpagiri temple complex dating to the 7th century, this temple honors Shiva as the divine healer.
highlight: The multi-temple complex on the sacred Pushpagiri hill.
entryNotes: Multiple temples within the Pushpagiri complex.

moreDetails.history: Founded around the 7th century CE, the complex includes seven Shiva temples.
moreDetails.architecture: Chalukyan-era stone temples in a hilltop setting.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Near Cuddapah town, easily accessible by road.

name: Bhimeswara Swamy Temple (Draksharama)
story: One of the five Pancharama Kshetras, this temple is believed to enshrine a fragment of Tarakasura's linga destroyed by Lord Kumara.
highlight: Intricate Chalukyan-era carvings and the massive sanctum.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Also an Ashta Dasha Shakti Peetha.

moreDetails.history: Built during the Chalukya period (7th-8th century), it is both a Pancharama Kshetra and a Shakti Peetha.
moreDetails.architecture: Blend of Chalukyan and Chola styles with elaborate friezes.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: The temple complex includes shrines for Manikyamba Devi.

name: Shiva Temple
story: A serene Shiva temple in the Galiveedu area, known for its peaceful environment.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: Good for a short spiritual stop.

name: Parasurameswara Swamy Temple
story: Housing one of the oldest known Shiva lingas in the world (2nd-3rd century BCE), depicting Shiva in a realistic hunter form.
highlight: The ancient, realistic Phallic Linga with a standing Shiva figure purely carved on it.
entryNotes: A site of immense archaeological importance.

moreDetails.history: The linga dates back to the 2nd or 3rd century BCE, making it one of the earliest surviving Hindu icons.
moreDetails.architecture: Apsidal (Gajaprishta) shrine typical of early Buddhist and Hindu structures.

name: Someswara Swamy Temple
story: An important Shiva temple near Bhimavaram, known for its sacred tank and local annual festivals.
highlight: The large temple tank and festival celebrations.
entryNotes: Distinct from the Pancharama Somarama (also in Bhimavaram).

moreDetails.history: Serves the Gunupudi locality of Bhimavaram.

name: Doddeswara Swamy Temple
story: An ancient temple with an imposing 8-foot Nandi carved from black basalt granite and a 6-foot linga in the sanctum.
highlight: The massive black basalt Nandi and the large Shiva linga.
entryNotes: Hemavathi was an ancient Pallava capital.

moreDetails.history: Built during the Pallava and Nolamba period (8th-11th century) in the former capital.
moreDetails.architecture: An 8-foot black basalt Nandi guards the 6-foot Shiva linga.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Hemavathi has several ancient temples worth exploring.

name: Shiva Temple
story: Located on the banks of the Bahuda river at the AP-Odisha border.

name: Tripuranthaka Swamy Temple
story: A 1000-year-old temple where the linga was found by a farmer ploughing the field, believed to be self-manifested.
highlight: The ancient history and the serene temple tank.
entryNotes: Located on the banks of the Gosthani river.

moreDetails.history: Historically significant temple in the region.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Jami is a peaceful village location.

name: Shiva Temple
story: Located in the historic town of Jammalamadugu near the Gandikota canyon.
highlight: The proximity to the 'Grand Canyon of India'.

moreDetails.history: Jammalamadugu has a rich history connected to Gandikota fort.

name: Sri Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple
story: Constructed in 1150 CE, this temple is dedicated to Mallikarjuna Swamy alongside Kamakshi Tai.
highlight: The 12th-century heritage and dual deity worship.

moreDetails.history: Built in 1150 CE, one of the important medieval Shiva temples of Rayalaseema.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Combined with Kamakshi Tai temple in the same complex.

name: Kailasakona Cave Temple
story: A scenic temple near a perennial waterfall, believe to be the place where Lord Kailasanatha performed penance.
highlight: The crystal clear waterfall cascading near the temple.

moreDetails.history: Legend links it to the wedding of Venkateswara and Padmavathi.

name: Bugga Rameswara Swamy Temple
story: Known for a perennial water spring (Bugga) in the sanctum, believed to have been installed by Lord Rama.
highlight: The natural spring water flowing around the Shiva Linga.

moreDetails.history: Legends connect it to Parasurama and Rama.
moreDetails.architecture: Traditional style in a scenic valley.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Can be combined with a visit to the rock formations nearby.

name: Shiva Temple
story: A historic temple in Kamalapuram, near the Papaghni river.

name: Manikanteswara Swamy Temple
story: Situated within the famous Kanipakam Vinayaka temple complex, this ancient Shiva temple dates back to the Chola period.
highlight: The Chola-era architecture and historical significance.
entryNotes: Visited along with the swayambhu Vinayaka.

moreDetails.history: Built by Kulothunga Chola I in the 11th century.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Kanipakam is famous for truth-swearing vows.

name: Sri Trikoteswara Swamy Temple
story: Perched on the three-peaked Trikuta Hill, this sacred shrine offers panoramic views and a challenging pilgrimage climb.
highlight: The three-peaked hill and the sweeping views from the summit.
entryNotes: Involves a steep hill climb; steps available.

moreDetails.history: An ancient pilgrimage center on the three-peaked Trikutachalam hill.
moreDetails.architecture: Temple complex spread across multiple peaks.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Massive Shivaratri celebrations draw lakhs of devotees.

name: Someswara Swamy Temple
story: Often considered a Kumararama Kshetra, this temple stands on the banks of the Gautami Godavari and is known for the Koteswara Lingam.
highlight: The sacred Godavari river ghats and the ancient linga.
entryNotes: Access often involves crossing the river by boat/ferry.

moreDetails.history: Ancient temple associated with the moon god (Soma) and Lord Indra.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: The temple tank and river confluence are sacred.

name: Rupala Sangameswara Swamy Temple
story: A magnificent temple usually submerged in the Srisailam backwaters, resurfacing only when water levels drop in summer.
highlight: The rare sighting of the temple when it emerges from the water.
entryNotes: Check water levels before planning; boat access required sometimes.

moreDetails.history: Ancient temple at the confluence of seven rivers (Saptaranadi Sangamam).
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Located near the shore but requires low water levels for full darshan.

name: Shiva Temple
story: The main Shiva temple in Lakkireddipalli, acting as a center for community gatherings and worship.

name: Veerabhadra Temple
story: A Vijayanagara masterpiece famous for its hanging pillar, monolithic Nandi, and stunning ceiling murals depicting Puranic scenes.
highlight: The hanging pillar and the massive monolithic Nandi bull.

moreDetails.history: Built in the 16th century by Virupanna and Veeranna, governors under the Vijayanagara Empire.
moreDetails.architecture: Outstanding Vijayanagara style with 70 carved pillars and ceiling murals.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: The hanging pillar that does not fully rest on the ground is a major attraction.

name: Mahanandi Temple
story: Set in the Nallamala foothills, this temple is famous for its nine Nandis and perennial freshwater spring pools.
highlight: Crystal-clear spring water emerging from the Nandi's mouth.
entryNotes: Bathing in the sacred pools is customary before darshan.

moreDetails.history: An ancient temple complex with nine Nandis and natural spring-fed pushkarinis.
moreDetails.architecture: Traditional Dravidian temple surrounded by lush gardens.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Part of the Nava Nandi pilgrimage circuit.

name: Mahendragiri Shiva Temple
story: Situated on the Mahendragiri peak (Eastern Ghats), associated with the Pandavas and Parasurama. It has shrines for Shiva and Gokarneswara.
highlight: The high-altitude setting and mythological connections.
entryNotes: Requires a trek or off-road drive.

moreDetails.history: Ancient site mentioned in the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
moreDetails.architecture: Ancient stone structures using cyclopean masonry styles.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: The highest peak in the Eastern Ghats of Odsha/Andhra border region.

name: Mandeswara Swamy Temple
story: Famous as a temple for Saturn (Saneeswara), where Shiva is worshipped to ward off planetary doshas.
highlight: The Saneeswara shrine and the tail-oil abhishekam.

moreDetails.history: Legend links it to the sage Dadichi and the demon heavy metal bone weapon.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Devotees flock here for relief from Saturn's influence.

name: Matsyalingeswara Swamy Temple
story: Famous for the sacred fish in the Machkund river pool that are protected and fed by devotees.
highlight: Feeding the large majestic mahseer fish in the temple pool.

moreDetails.history: Ancient tribal shrine with unique ecological traditions.

name: Mogileeswara Swamy Temple
story: Known as Dakshina Kasi, famous for the Nandi from whose mouth water flows perpetually.
highlight: The magical spring water flowing from Nandi's mouth.

moreDetails.history: Ancient temple with renovations by Chola and Pallava kings.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: A popular stopover for pilgrims traveling to Tirupati.

name: Shiva Temple
story: Serves the spiritual needs of the Muddanur railway town community.

name: Kshana Mukteswara Swamy Temple
story: Legend says that even a moment's (kshana) worship here grants liberation (mukti).
highlight: The belief in instant liberation and the riverbank setting.
entryNotes: A serene temple on the Godavari bank.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: Located in the scenic Konaseema region.

name: Bhimeswara Swamy Temple
story: A historic Shiva temple serving the local community for centuries.

name: Veereswara Swamy Temple
story: Famous for the daily celestial wedding (Nitya Kalyanam) performed for Veereswara and Bhadrakali.
highlight: The Nitya Kalyanam ritual performed every night.
timings: Open daily; evening best for Kalyanam.
entryNotes: Advance booking for Kalyanam seva is advised.

moreDetails.history: Ancient temple where the goddess is Bhadrakali.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Muramalla is known for fulfilling marriage-related wishes.

name: Shiva Temple
story: Located at the busy Mydukur junction, this temple offers a spiritual respite for travelers and locals.

name: Sri Moolastaneswara Swamy Temple
story: An ancient 11th-century Shiva temple in Mulapeta, Nellore, with multiple subsidiary shrines within the complex.
highlight: The ancient 11th-century heritage and the Sahasra Lingeswara shrine.
entryNotes: Located in Mulapeta area of Nellore city.

moreDetails.history: Dating to the 11th century with subsidiary shrines for Vinayaka, Subrahmanya, and Kala Bhairava.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: In the heart of Nellore city.

name: Malleswara Swamy Temple
story: A significant local temple dedicated to Malleswara Swamy, serving the spiritual needs of Nossam and surrounding villages.
highlight: The traditional rituals and local festivals.

moreDetails.history: Local history dates back several centuries.

name: Ksheerarama Temple
story: One of the Pancharama Kshetras, legend holds that Lord Vishnu received the Sudarshana Chakra from Shiva here in an ocean of milk.
highlight: One of the tallest temple towers in Andhra Pradesh.
entryNotes: A prominent pilgrimage destination in the Godavari delta.

moreDetails.history: Ancient Pancharama Kshetra where Vishnu is said to have obtained the Sudarshana Chakra.
moreDetails.architecture: Dravidian style with one of the tallest gopurams in AP.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Palakollu is in the fertile Godavari delta region.

name: Kasi Visweswara Swamy Temple
story: Famous for the 'Kasi Bugga' or water spring, giving the town its name (Kasibugga).
highlight: The natural spring associated with Kasi Visweswara.

moreDetails.history: Named after the spring (Bugga) and Kasi (Varanasi).

name: Sri Panikeswara Swamy Temple
story: An ancient Shiva temple in Panyam nestled near the Nallamala range, blending natural beauty with devotion.
entryNotes: Near Mahanandi; can be combined as one trip.

moreDetails.history: An ancient temple in the Nava Nandi pilgrimage region.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Part of the Nava Nandi group near Mahanandi.

name: Veerabhadra Swamy Temple
story: Picturesquely located on a hillock on an island in the Godavari River, dedicated to Veerabhadra.
highlight: The boat ride to the island and the scenic hillock setting.
entryNotes: Must take a boat to reach the temple.

moreDetails.history: Ancient hill temple on a river island.
moreDetails.architecture: Traditional style adapted to the hill terrain.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: The surrounding Papikondalu hills add to the beauty.

name: Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple
story: A renowned temple famous for Rahu-Ketu puja, believed to have been installed by the sage Bharadwaja.
highlight: The Rahu-Ketu dosha nivarana pujas performed here.
entryNotes: Very busy on Rahu Kalam timings.

moreDetails.history: Ancient temple rebuilt in later periods.

name: Sri Kukkuteswara Swamy Temple
story: An ancient Shiva temple and one of the Ashta Dasha Shakti Peethas, where Pada Gaya Kshetra rituals are performed.
highlight: The Ashta Dasha Shakti Peetha status and the Pada Gaya Kshetra.
entryNotes: Pada Gaya Kshetra rituals are popular here.

moreDetails.history: Ancient temple associated with a rooster (kukkuta) legend and Shakti Peetha traditions.
moreDetails.architecture: Traditional Dravidian temple complex with multiple shrines.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Pithapuram is an important pilgrimage town in East Godavari.

name: Agastyeswara Swamy Temple
story: Located on the banks of the Penna River, this temple is believed to have been consecrated by Sage Agastya.
highlight: The riverside location and the association with Sage Agastya.
entryNotes: Proddatur is known as the Second Bombay for its gold business.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: The Dasara celebrations here are famous.

name: Shiva Temple
story: A prominent place of worship in Pulivendula town.

name: Uma Kotilingeswara Swamy Temple
story: A famous cave temple located in the Eastern Ghats, where a perennial waterfall bathes the Shiva Linga.
highlight: The linga bathed by a natural waterfall inside the cave.

moreDetails.history: Ancient pilgrimage site in the hills.

name: Trikuteswara Swamy Temple
story: Part of the Pushpagiri complex, this temple features a triple shrine (Trikuta) dedicated to Shiva.
entryNotes: Explore the entire complex of temples.

moreDetails.history: Built during the Vijayanagara and earlier periods.
moreDetails.architecture: Trikuta style common in Chalukya/Kakatiya architecture.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Pushpagiri is often called the Hampi of Kadapa.

name: Kotilingeswara Swamy Temple
story: Legend says Ravana worshipped Shiva here. The temple is famed for the belief that it was once the site of ten million (koti) lingas.
highlight: The Kotilingala Ghat and the river view.

moreDetails.history: Historically significant ghat temple traditionally linked to Ravana.

name: Markandeya Swamy Temple
story: Located in the heart of Rajahmundry near the Godavari ghats, believed to have been consecrated by Sage Markandeya.
highlight: Its central location near the Pushkar Ghat.

moreDetails.history: Rebuilt in 1818 after earlier structures, it stands where Markandeya is said to have been saved by Shiva.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Close to the Godavari river bathing ghats.

name: Endala Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple
story: Known for the miracle where no shadow falls on the deity, and people suffering from skin diseases are believed to be cured here.
highlight: The belief in curing skin ailments and the sunny location.
entryNotes: Devotees leave their old clothes here after a cure.

moreDetails.history: Ancient folklore connects it to the Pandavas.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Specifically famous for dermatological healing beliefs.

name: Veerabhadra Swamy Temple
story: A major pilgrimage center where Veerabhadra is worshipped as the presiding deity. Known as Dakshina Kailasam.
highlight: The unique custom of sun rays falling on the idol in March.
entryNotes: Sun rays illuminate the idol for 5 days in March.

moreDetails.history: Ancient temple patronized by Kakatiyas and Vijayanagara kings.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Located in the heart of Rayachoti town.

name: Sadasiva Swamy Temple
story: Located atop a hill amidst waterfalls and dense vegetation, known for its serene and powerful ambience.
highlight: The panoramic hill views and cascading water.
entryNotes: Known for its curative herbs and water.

moreDetails.history: Ancient hill shrine frequented by locals.

name: Kumararama Bhimeswara Swamy Temple
story: Built by the Eastern Chalukya king Chalukya Bhima I, this Pancharama Kshetra is named after Lord Kumara (Kartikeya).
highlight: The ancient Chalukyan stone architecture and carved pillars.

moreDetails.history: Constructed by Chalukya Bhima I in the 9th century, it is ASI-protected heritage.
moreDetails.architecture: Eastern Chalukyan style with ornate stone carvings.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Near Kakinada, well connected by road and rail.

name: Sangameswara Temple
story: At the sacred confluence of the Nagavali, Suvarnamukhi, and Vegavati rivers, this temple is one of the five linga kshetras.
highlight: The holy tri-river confluence beside the temple.

moreDetails.history: An ancient linga kshetra at the confluence of three rivers.
moreDetails.architecture: Traditional temple at a scenic river junction.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Bathing at the sangam is considered highly auspicious.

name: Ramalingeswara Swamy Temple
story: An ancient Chola-era temple in Santharavuru, reflecting the deep Shaivite roots of the coastal region.
highlight: The historical antiquity of the temple structure.

name: Ramalingeswara Swamy Temple
story: An old Shiva temple frequented by locals in the Srikakulam region.

name: Siddhavateswara Swamy Temple
story: Located within the historic Siddhavatam Fort on the banks of the Penna River, known as 'Dakshina Kasi'.
highlight: The location inside a medieval fort and the river ghats.
entryNotes: Must explore the fort ruins as well.

moreDetails.history: An ancient temple that gave the fort its spiritual significance.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Siddhavatam is often called the Gateway to Srisailam.

name: Someswara Swamy Temple
story: A historic temple relocated due to the Somasila project, dedicated to Someswara.
highlight: The scenic Somasila dam and reservoir backdrop.

moreDetails.history: Ancient temple shifted to higher ground.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Popular picnic spot due to the dam.

name: Someswara Swamy Temple
story: A prominent Shiva temple in the northernmost part of AP, reflecting Odia-Andhra cultural blend.

name: Sri Kalahasteeswara Temple
story: The element 'Air.' The flickering lamp in the windless sanctum proves the presence of the Air element.
entryNotes: Very famous for Rahu Ketu remedial prayers.

moreDetails.history: Associated with Kannappa Nayanar, who offered his eyes to the Lord.

name: Srikalahasteeswara Temple
story: Known as the Kailasa of South India, this temple enshrines the Vayu Linga, representing the element of air. The lamp inside the sanctum flickers without wind.
highlight: The eternally flickering lamp in the windless sanctum.
entryNotes: Famous for Rahu-Ketu puja performed here.

moreDetails.history: Ancient temple mentioned in Shaiva texts, one of the Pancha Bhuta Sthalams representing air.
moreDetails.architecture: Massive gopuram with Vijayanagara-era additions and a 36-meter tall tower.

name: Srimukhalingam Temple
story: One of India's oldest Shiva temples, unique for depicting three forms of Shiva — Mukhalingeswara, Bhimeswara, and Someswara.
highlight: The three Shiva forms and the lingam with facial features.
entryNotes: Remote location; plan transport in advance.

moreDetails.history: Built by the Eastern Ganga king Kamarnava II in the 8th century AD.
moreDetails.architecture: Kalinga and Dravidian architectural fusion with intricate carvings.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: A trickle of water constantly flows from the middle face of the lingam.

name: Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple
story: Nestled in the Nallamala Hills on the banks of the Krishna River, this ancient shrine is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and a Shakti Peetha.
highlight: The forested hilltop setting and the river gorge views from the temple.
timings: 6:00 AM to 3:30 PM and 6:00 PM to 10:00 PM.
entryNotes: Road access through forest routes can be seasonal.

moreDetails.history: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas and an ancient Shakti Peetha, the temple is mentioned in inscriptions from the 2nd century onward.
moreDetails.architecture: Dravidian style with large gopurams and a fortified complex on a hilltop.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Srisailam is surrounded by the Nallamala forest and tiger reserve.

name: Pallikondeswara Swamy Temple
story: A unique temple where Lord Shiva is depicted in a reclining posture (Sayana Shiva), resting on Goddess Parvati's lap after consuming Halahala poison.
highlight: The rare idol of Shiva sleeping on Parvati's lap.
entryNotes: Located on the AP-Tamil Nadu border.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: Devotees believe this is where Shiva rested after the churning of the ocean.

name: Bugga Ramalingeswara Swamy Temple
story: A hidden gem admired for its incredibly detailed stone carvings rivaling those of Hampi and Belur.
highlight: The astonishingly intricate stone carvings on every surface.
entryNotes: Located in Tadipatri town, easy to access.

moreDetails.history: A 15th-century Vijayanagara-era temple known for its exceptionally fine carvings.
moreDetails.architecture: Vijayanagara style with extraordinary sculptural detail.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Often compared to Hampi for the quality of its stone work.

name: Siddheswara Swamy Temple (Talakona)
story: Set amidst the dense Seshachalam forests near the spectacular Talakona waterfall.
highlight: The stunning 270-foot waterfall and forest setting.
timings: Open daily; forest entry restricted at night.
entryNotes: Involves a trek through the forest.

moreDetails.history: Ancient forest shrine revered by sages.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Talakona is the highest waterfall in Andhra Pradesh.

name: Shiva Temple
story: A historic Shiva temple in Tekkali, preserving the region's traditions.

name: Kapila Theertham Temple
story: The only Shiva temple in Tirupati, nestled beside a waterfall, associated with the sage Kapila's penance.
highlight: The natural waterfall cascading beside the temple.
bestTime: Monsoon for the waterfall; winter for pleasant weather.
entryNotes: Waterfall may dry up in summer.

moreDetails.history: Ancient temple associated with the sage Kapila, at the foot of Tirumala Hills.
moreDetails.architecture: Dravidian temple built against the hillside with a natural waterfall.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Located at the foot of the Tirumala Hills, close to Tirupati town.

name: Sri Tripurantakeswara Temple
story: Named after Shiva as Tripurantaka, the destroyer of the three flying cities (Tripura), this temple sits on a scenic hilltop.
highlight: The Tripura legend connection and the hilltop views.

moreDetails.history: Ancient temple associated with the Tripurantaka form of Shiva.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Combined with Bala Tripurasundari shrine at the same location.

name: Ramalingeswara Swamy Temple
story: An ancient Shiva temple in Velpuru/Tanuku region, reflecting the rich Shaivite traditions of the Godavari delta.
highlight: The peaceful ambience and traditional rituals.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: A good example of a rural Godavari temple.

name: Shiva Temple
story: The principal Shiva temple in Vempalli, reflecting the devotional culture of the Rayalaseema region.

name: Malleswara Swamy Temple
story: Located on the Indrakeeladri hill adjacent to the famous Kanaka Durga temple, dating back to the 10th century.
highlight: The view of the Krishna river and city from the hill.
entryNotes: Part of the Kanaka Durga temple complex visit.

moreDetails.history: Installed by Yudhishthira of the Pandavas, according to legend.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Can be visited along with Kanaka Durga temple.

name: Visweswara Swamy Temple
story: Located near the Coastal Battery, this temple is a popular worship site in Vizag city.
highlight: The proximity to the sea and RK Beach.
entryNotes: Easy access from RK Beach road.

moreDetails.history: Modern era temple with traditional rituals.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Can be visited during a beach outing.

name: Sri Yaganti Uma Maheshwara Temple
story: Dating to the 5th century, this cave temple is famous for its growing Nandi idol and unique Ardhanareeswara carved from a single stone.
highlight: The mysteriously growing Nandi idol and the natural cave shrine.
entryNotes: Located in a hilly area; comfortable footwear advised.

moreDetails.history: Dates to the 5th-6th century with contributions from Pallavas, Cholas, Chalukyas, and Vijayanagara rulers.
moreDetails.architecture: Rock-cut cave temple with a naturally formed Ardhanareeswara idol.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: The Nandi idol here is scientifically documented to be slowly growing.

name: Uma Maheswara Swamy Temple
story: An ancient temple with Chola-era inscriptions, reflecting the region's rich history.
highlight: The detailed inscriptions and ancient architecture.

moreDetails.history: Built during the Chola administration of Cuddapah region.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Of interest to history and epigraphy enthusiasts.

name: Lalamati Duramari Ganesh-Shiva
story: An archaeological site revealing ancient temples of Shiva and Ganesh.

name: Siddheswar Temple (Badarpur)
story: Situated on the bank of the Barak river; believed to be established by Sage Kapila.

name: Madan Kamdev
story: Archaeological site with ruins of 10-12th century temples depicting erotic art; main deity is Uma-Maheshwar.

name: Barpeta Road Shiva Mandir
story: The central Shiva temple in the bustling business hub of Barpeta Road.

name: Billeswar Temple
story: An ancient temple where a Shiva Linga was found underground while digging for 'Bel' roots.

name: Biswanath Ghat
story: Known as 'Gupta Kashi'; many ancient temples are submerged in the Brahmaputra during summer.

name: Lankeshwar Temple (Bongaigaon)
story: Another temple nameLankeshwar, situated on a hillock in Bongaigaon.

name: Tilinga Mandir
story: The 'Bell Temple'; devotees tie bells to the Banyan tree for wish fulfillment. Thousands of bells hang here.

name: Negheriting Shiva Doul
story: A magnificent temple built on a hillock; famous for its resident rhesus monkeys. Follows Panchayatana style.

name: Gopeswar Temple
story: Situated at the foot of Deuduar hill; ancient temple surrounded by nature.

name: Gupteswar Temple (Dhekiajuli)
story: Another Gupteswar temple in the region, often confused with Singri but distinct presence in local lore.

name: Ghuguha Doul
story: Built by Queen Phuleswari; legend associates it with a bamboo grove (Ghuguha) protecting a linga.

name: Chitalmari Shiva Mandir
story: An old Shiva temple located near Dhing in Nagaon.

name: Kirateswar Temple
story: Associated with the Kirata people and their worship of Shiva; an ancient site in Western Assam.

name: Shiva Mandir (Digboi)
story: A prominent Shiva temple in the historic oil town of Digboi.

name: Shiva Mandir (Diphu)
story: The main Shiva temple in Diphu, the headquarters of Karbi Anglong.

name: Parihareswar Devalaya
story: Known for the Devadasi dance tradition (Nati-Nritya) of Assam; very significant cultural center.

name: Dudhnoi Shiva Temple
story: A significant local temple in the Dudhnoi town.

name: Shiva Mandir (Duliajan)
story: A prominent temple in the oil township of Duliajan.

name: Garampani Shiva Temple
story: Located near the Garampani Wildlife Sanctuary; famous for hot water springs and a Shiva temple.

name: Shiva Dol (Gaurisagar)
story: Built by Queen Phuleswari Devi. The Shiva Dol here is the central temple of the group.

name: Sri Surya Pahar (Shiva Lingas)
story: Archaeological site said to contain 99,999 Shiva Lingas, second only to Kashi.

name: Thakkerswari Temple
story: Located on the bank of Brahmaputra; dedicated to Shiva and Shakti.

name: Gohpur Shiva Mandir
story: An important Shiva temple in the historic town of Gohpur.

name: Goreswar Temple
story: Dedicated to the 'White Lord' (Goreswar); located on the banks of river Puthimari.

name: Mahadev Sal
story: Patronized by the Gouripur Zamindars; located under ancient Sal trees.

name: Baneswar Temple
story: An old temple in the city, associated with King Bana.

name: Basistha Temple
story: Ashram of Sage Basistha; features streams (Sandhya, Lalita, Kanta) and a Shiva temple.

name: Bhootnath Temple
story: Located in the heart of the city's main cremation ground; Shiva is worshipped here as Bhootnath (Lord of Ghosts).

name: Chakreshwar Temple
story: Located at Kalipur; famous for a giant chakra impression on rock, but houses a Shiva temple.

name: Lankeswar Temple
story: Located atop a hill near Gauhati University; legend says Ravana worshipped Shiva here.

name: Narakasur Hill Shiva
story: Associated with the mythological King Narakasura; an ancient Shiva shrine exists here.

name: Navagraha Temple
story: Located on Chitrachal Hill; dedicated to the nine celestial bodies with Shiva (Surya) at the center.

name: Sukreswar Temple
story: Built by Ahom King Pramatta Singha; located on the Itakhuli hillock on the Brahmaputra bank.

name: Umananda Temple
story: Located on the Peacock Island in the Brahmaputra; where Lord Shiva burnt Kamadeva to ashes.

name: Urvashi Island Ruins
story: An island (sometimes submerged) with ancient rock carvings of Vishnu and Shiva.

name: Shiva Mandir (Haflong)
story: A serene temple in Assam's only hill station, Haflong.

name: Kameswar Temple
story: Dedicated to Shiva as the dissolver of Kama (Desire). King Pramatta Singha built the current structure.

name: Kedareswar Temple
story: Located on Madanachala Hill; houses a Swayambhu Linga of Ardhanarishwara form.

name: Deosal Shiva Temple
story: Legend says Sita lived here in Valmiki's ashram. An ancient Shiva temple exists here.

name: Sitajakhala
story: Features ancient rock-cut steps leading to the Brahmaputra, believed to be used by Sita. Many Shiva lingas found.

name: Nagshankar Temple
story: Famous for its pond filled with rare turtles and huge fish; dedicated to Nagshankar (Shiva).

name: Pancharatna Shiva Temple
story: Located on Pancharatna Hill near the Naranarayan Setu; famous for rock-cut shrines and a Shiva temple.

name: Borbheti Shiva Than
story: A significant historical Than built by the Ahom kings, dedicated to Lord Shiva.

name: Hatigarh Shiva Doul
story: Built by Ahom King Pramatta Singha. Located near the Hatigarh (Elephant stable).

name: Pingaleswar Temple
story: Famous for its association with Pingala; a significant rural Shiva temple.

name: Badulikurung Shiva Mandir
story: An ancient shrine reportedly frequented by bats (Baduli).

name: Khairabari Shiva Mandir
story: A central place of worship for the Khairabari region.

name: Khaspur Snan Mandir
story: Part of the Kachari kingdom ruins; the Snan Mandir was used for royal baths/worship.

name: Shiva Mandir (Kokrajhar)
story: The central Shiva temple for the Kokrajhar town.

name: Maibong Shiva Temple
story: A monolithic rock-cut temple in the Mahur river, dating back to the Kachari kingdom capital.

name: Shiva Mandir (Mangaldai)
story: A significant temple in the historic Darrang district.

name: Shiva Mandir (Margherita)
story: The main Shiva temple of the coal town Margherita, nestled in the Patkai hills.

name: Kalyan Mandir
story: A prominent local Shiva temple in Morigaon town.

name: Sidheswar Devalaya (Nagaon)
story: An ancient Shiva temple in the Nagaon district with Tantric roots.

name: Nagrijuli Shiva Mandir
story: Known for ancient stone ruins and connection to the phrase 'Nagar-Juli' (Stream of city).

name: Ganga Pukhuri Shiva Temple
story: Located near the historic Ganga Pukhuri; hosts a major fair during Ashok Astami.

name: Shiva Mandir (Namrup)
story: Located in the industrial town of Namrup; a center for local workforce devotion.

name: Garakhiya Doul
story: Associated with cowherds (Garakhiya); a small octagonal temple built by Ahom kings.

name: Manikarneswar Temple
story: A star-shaped temple on a hillock; offers panoramic views of the Brahmaputra.

name: Nandi Keshwar Temple
story: Dedicated to Nandi, the bull of Shiva, but houses a Shiva linga as well.

name: Shiva Doul (North Lakhimpur)
story: The central Shiva temple of North Lakhimpur town.

name: Deopahar
story: Ancient temple ruins on a hill amidst Deopahar forest; known for intricate stone carvings and Tantric history

name: Panimur Shiva Temple
story: Situated by the Kopili river waterfalls; a breathtaking location with a Shiva temple.

name: Pathsala Shiva Mandir
story: A prominent temple in Pathsala, the educational hub of Bajali.

name: Rangapara Shiva Mandir
story: Located in the railway town of Rangapara, surrounded by tea gardens.

name: Bura-Buri Than
story: A sacred spot for the Chutiya kingdom and local tribes; worshipping Shiva and Shakti as the old couple (Bura-Buri).

name: Bhuban Pahar Temple
story: Located on the Bhuban Hill; a very significant pilgrimage site in Barak Valley. Requires a tough trek.

name: Singri Gupta Temple
story: Dedicated to Gupteswar Shiva; legend says it was built by Vishwakarma himself. Situated near the Brahmaputra.

name: Rangnath Dol
story: Located near the Rang Ghar; dedicated to Shiva. Built by Rudra Singha.

name: Shiva Dol (Sivasagar)
story: The tallest Shiva temple in India (height 104 ft), built by Queen Ambika on the banks of Sivasagar tank.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: Visit Vishnu and Devi Dols too.

name: Siddheswar Devalaya
story: Located in the 'Manchester of Assam' (Silk village); renovated by Ahom King Shiva Singha.

name: Bamun Pahar Ruins
story: Famous for exquisite stone carvings and pillars of an ancient temple complex devoted to Shiva.

name: Da Parbatia
story: Famous for its 6th-century door frame depicting Gupta art, the finest early specimen in Assam. Originally a Shiva temple.

name: Haleswar Temple
story: A Shiva linga found by a farmer while ploughing (Hal); hence named Haleswar.

name: Ketakeshwar Dewal
story: Houses one of the largest Swayambhu Lingams in the world, originally found in a bamboo grove.

name: Maha Bhairav Temple
story: Believed to be established by King Bana (as per mythology). Houses one of the largest Shiva Lingams.

name: Rudrapad Temple
story: Houses the footprint (Pad) of Rudra (Shiva) in a stone; located on the Brahmaputra bank.

name: Tingewsar Temple
story: An old Shiva temple site in the Sonitpur district, rich in archaeological value.

name: Tihu Shiva Mandir
story: A significant Shiva temple located in the town of Tihu.

name: Na-Pukhuri Shiva Dol
story: Located by the Na-Pukhuri (New Pond) dug by King Sarbananda Singha; features a Shiva Dol.

name: Bhairabkunda Shiva Mandir
story: Located at the tri-junction of Bhutan, Assam, and Arunachal; a popular Shiva temple in a scenic spot.

name: Haringi Shiva Mandir
story: A Shiva temple treasured by the local communities in Udalguri.

name: Ambika Bhawani
story: Believed to be the site of Daksha's Yagna where Sati immolated herself. It is a major Shakti Peeth with a Bhairav (Shiva) shrine.
highlight: The mythological site of Sati's sacrifice.

name: Someshwar Nath Temple
story: A 2000-year-old temple housing a rare Panchmukhi (five-faced) Shivalinga. Lord Rama is believed to have worshipped here.
highlight: The 55-feet tall temple and the five-faced Swayambhu Lingam.

name: Baikatpur Gauri Shankar
story: An ancient temple dedicated to the combined form of Shiva and Parvati (Gauri-Shankar). Located in the rural outskirts of Patna.

name: Siddheshwar Nath Temple
story: Perched on the highest peak of the Barabar Hills, this ancient Shiva temple offers panoramic views and is near the famous Ashokan caves.
highlight: The trek to the top and the ancient caves nearby.

name: Sidhanath Temple
story: Located on the banks of the Karmanasa River, this temple is popularly known as Baba Ratan Puri Temple.
highlight: The riverside setting and local legends.

name: Mahadeva Shiv Mandir
story: Considered one of the oldest Shiva temples in the Gopalganj region, attracting devotees from far and wide.
highlight: The ancient Lingam and the sanctity.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: Main Shiva temple of the area.

name: Alakhnath Temple
story: Another significant temple in Barh, associated with Naga Sadhus and the 'Alakh Niranjan' tradition.
highlight: The association with ascetics and the river.

name: Umnath Temple
story: A historic temple on the banks of the Ganges. Legends say Goddess Parvati (Uma) worshipped Shiva here.
highlight: The scenic ghats and the ancient idol.

name: Baneshwar Sthan
story: An ancient temple believed to be established by the mythological King Banasur. It is a center of deep faith in the Mithila region.
highlight: The connection to King Banasur and the ancient Lingam.

name: Baba Koteshwarnath Temple
story: Located at the confluence of Morhar and Dargha rivers. It features a unique Sahasra Linga (1008 miniature Lingas carved on one).
highlight: The Sahasra Linga and the river confluence.

name: Dhaneshwar Nath Mahadev
story: Also known as Gaurishankar Mahadev Sthan, it is a significant center of worship in the Jhanjharpur subdivision.

name: Baba Budhanath Temple
story: Also known as Vridhheshwar Nath, it is one of the oldest temples in Bhagalpur, situated on the banks of the river Ganga.
highlight: The serene ghats and the ancient Lingam.

name: Bhairava Ugna Mahadev
story: Another significant temple dedicated to the Ugna incarnation of Shiva, located in the Bisfi block, the birthplace of Vidyapati.
highlight: The literary heritage of Bisfi and Vidyapati.

name: Ugna Mahadev Mandir
story: The site where Lord Shiva, in the guise of a servant named Ugna, revealed his true form to the great poet Vidyapati.
highlight: The deep literary and spiritual connection to Vidyapati.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: A pilgrimage for literature lovers too.

name: Bhimbandh Temple
story: Located in the Bhimbandh Wildlife Sanctuary, known for its hot springs. Legend says Bhima built a dam (bandh) here. There are old Shiva shrines.
highlight: The hot springs and the forest setting.

name: Mandar Hill Temple
story: Located on Mandar Hill, legendary for being the churning rod in Samudra Manthan. It has temples for Shiva, Vishnu, and Jain Tirthankaras.
highlight: The mythological significance of the hill and the views.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: Take the ropeway for easy access.

name: Brahmeshwar Nath Temple
story: A historic temple famous for its west-facing door, which legend says turned to defy Mahmood Ghazni. It hosts a massive cattle fair.
highlight: The west-facing sanctum and the legend of the turning temple.

name: Shri Adinath Akhara
story: An ashram and temple complex dedicated to Lord Shiva, following the Nath tradition. Located near the Buxar railway station.
highlight: The Akhara tradition and spiritual atmosphere.

name: Charaut Math
story: A historic Math (monastic establishment) which houses a prominent Shiva temple. It has a rich tradition of ascetics.
highlight: The monastic tradition and the old temple structure.

name: Katyayani Sthan
story: A major Shakti Peeth dedicated to Goddess Katyayani. As with all Shakti Peeths, it has a Bhairav (Shiva) shrine, integral to worship.
highlight: The connection to Goddess Durga and the river Kosi.

name: Dharmnath Mandir
story: A prominent Shiva temple in Chhapra town, known for its longevity and as a center of local religious activities.

name: Ahilya Sthan
story: The place where Ahilya, cursed to be a stone, was redeemed by Lord Rama. It is a major pilgrimage center with Shiva and Rama temples.

name: Mittheswarnath Shiv Temple
story: A revered Shiva temple in Darbhanga, known for its beautiful architecture and religious significance in Mithila.
highlight: The peaceful ambiance and traditional architecture.

name: Deo Sun Temple
story: A magnificent sun temple that is unique for facing west. While dedicated to Surya, it houses shrines for Shiva and is a major pilgrimage site.
highlight: The intricate stone architecture and the Chhath festival.

name: Baba Mukteshwarnath Temple
story: A significant Shiva temple located near the Bihar-Jharkhand border, often visited by pilgrims going to Deoghar.

name: Baba Khar Nath Temple
story: Built over the Samadhi of Baba Khar Nath, a saint who took living Samadhi. It is a major center of local faith.
highlight: The Samadhi shrine and the faith of locals.

name: Shiv Temple Dharhara
story: A revered Shiva temple in the Kosi region, considered a very holy place by the locals.
highlight: The spiritual atmosphere in a rural setting.

name: Brahmajuni Hill Temple
story: Known for the 1000 stone steps leading to the top, it has a clear view of Vishnupad. It houses ancient shrines including Shiva.
highlight: The panoramic view of Gaya and the ancient caves.

name: Markandey Mahadev
story: Dedicated to Lord Shiva as worshipped by Sage Markandeya. Devotees visit for longevity and health.

name: Pretshila Hill Temple
story: Located on Pretshila Hill, this temple is dedicated to Yamraj but also houses a Shiva shrine. It is crucial for Pind Daan rituals for accidental deaths.
highlight: The view of Gaya and the unique Pind Daan importance.

name: Ramshila Hill Temple
story: The Ramshila Hill houses the ancient Pataleshwar Mahadev temple along with temples for Rama and Sita.
highlight: The Pataleshwar shrine and the Ramayana connection.

name: Gorakhnath Temple
story: Dedicated to Guru Gorakhnath, a form of Shiva. It acts as a spiritual center for the Nath tradition followers in the region.
highlight: The Nath tradition and serene environment.

name: Gupteshwar Cave Temple
story: A natural limestone cave temple located in the Kaimur hills. It houses a natural stalagmite Shivalinga and is steeped in legends of Bhasmasura.
highlight: The adventurous trek and the natural cave formation.

name: Kaun Haara Ghat
story: The legendary site of the elephant (Gajendra) and crocodile fight, where Vishnu saved the elephant. It has Shiva and Vishnu temples.
highlight: The mythological struggle and liberation legend.

name: Pataleshwar Mandir
story: A historic temple where the Shivling is located below ground level inside a pit, hence the name Pataleshwar.

name: Ramchaura Mandir
story: Marking the spot where Lord Rama stayed on his way to Janakpur. It houses a Shivling believed to be worshipped by Rama.
highlight: The footprints of Lord Rama and the historic significance.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: A key religious site in Hajipur.

name: Giddheshwar Temple
story: Legend says this is where the mythical fight between Ravana and Jatayu took place. The temple is situated in a scenic hilly spot.
highlight: The Ramayana connection and the boulders.

name: Patneshwar Mandir
story: A scenic temple located near the Kiul river, established by the Goswami family. It is known for the mud wall that forms around the Lingam in Sawan.
highlight: The scenic location and the Sawan rituals.

name: Shilanath Mahadev Mandir
story: An ancient temple located in Dullipatti village near the Nepal border town of Jaynagar.
highlight: The proximity to the border and ancient roots.

name: Bateshwar Nath Temple
story: Located near the ancient Vikramshila University, this temple is associated with Sage Vashishta. The site also has ancient rock-cut caves.
highlight: The proximity to Vikramshila ruins and the Ganges.

moreDetails.history: Ancient site; Tantric Buddhism connection nearby.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Must visit Vikramshila University ruins nearby.

name: Shringirishi Dham
story: A beautiful spot in the hills where Sage Shringi (Rishya Sringa) medititated. It has a Shiva temple and a waterfall.
highlight: The natural beauty and the cave shrine.

name: Kakolat Waterfall Temple
story: A Shiva temple located at the base of the famous Kakolat waterfall. Legend says a king turned into a python was cursed here and attained salvation.
highlight: The cool waterfall and the scenic temple.

name: Viraat Ramayan Mandir
story: An under-construction temple complex set to be the world's largest Ramayan temple, featuring the world's largest Shivling.
highlight: The ambitious scale and the future largest Lingam.

name: Konch Shiva Temple
story: A magnificent ancient brick temple dating back to the later Gupta or early medieval period. It resembles the Deo Sun Temple and Bodh Gaya temple.
highlight: The curvilinear Sikhara and ancient brickwork.

name: Sundernath Dham
story: A famous Shiva temple located right on the India-Nepal border. It is a major pilgrimage site for people from both countries.
highlight: The cross-border devotion and the Sundari Math.

name: Kusheshwar Asthan
story: A major Shiva temple surrounded by wetlands which are a bird sanctuary. It is considered a 'Baba Dham' of Mithila.
highlight: The combination of pilgrimage and bird watching.

name: Ashok Dham Temple
story: Also known as Indradamneshwar Mahadev, this temple was discovered by a shepherd named Ashok. It houses a massive black stone Shivling.
highlight: The sheer size of the temple complex and the Lingam.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: Has temples for other deities too.

name: Madanpur Devi Temple
story: A revered Goddess temple in West Champaran, known for fulfilling wishes. It has a significant Shiva Lingam worshipped alongside the Devi.
highlight: The devotion of the local Tharu community.

name: Umga Shiva Temple
story: Part of the famous Umga Sun Temple complex, this temple houses Lord Shiva and is a masterpiece of stone architecture.
highlight: The majestic stone architecture on the hill.

moreDetails.history: Ancient; similar to Deo Sun Temple.

name: Karu Khirhari Temple
story: Dedicated to Sant Karu Khirhari, a great devotee of Shiva and protector of cows. He is worshipped as a divine figure in the Kosi region.
highlight: The folk deity tradition and cow worship.

name: Jaimangla Gadh
story: Located on an island in the Kabartal Lake, this temple is dedicated to Goddess Jaimangla (Durga). It features ancient Shiva shrines.
highlight: The location in the bird sanctuary lake.

name: Mahendranath Temple
story: Built by King Mahendra of Nepal, this temple is famous for its large pond and the tradition of offering clay bells.
highlight: The massive temple pond and hanging bells.

name: Khudneshwar Asthan
story: Named after a Muslim woman, Khudni, who discovered the Lingam. It is a unique symbol of Hindu-Muslim unity.
highlight: The story of Khudni Mai and the communal harmony.
entryNotes: Burial site of Khudni is inside.

name: Chandika Sthan
story: A Shakti Peeth where Sati's eye fell. It is associated with Karna of Mahabharata. A Shiva temple ensures the balance of energies.
highlight: The legend of Karna worshipping here.

name: Kastaharni Ghat Temple
story: Situated on the banks of the Ganges, this ghat has a Shiva temple believe to cure pains (Kasta-Harni). Lord Rama and Sita are said to have rested here.

name: Rishi Kund
story: Another hot spring site in Munger, believed to be the abode of sages. It has a Shiva temple amidst the hills.
highlight: The secluded nature spot and hot water.

name: Garib Nath Temple
story: Known as the 'Second Deoghar', this temple is the heart of Muzaffarpur. The Lingam appeared from a banyan tree.

moreDetails.history: Discovered by a landlord cutting a Banyan tree.

name: Dasshisha Nath Mahadev
story: Located in the middle of the Son River, believed to be established by Ravana. The Lingam remains submerged for 8 months a year.
highlight: The unique location inside the river.

name: Shobhnath Temple
story: An important Shiva temple in Nawada town, known for its spiritual ambiance and rituals.
highlight: The central role in Nawada's religious life.

name: Badi Patan Devi
story: One of the oldest and most sacred temples in Patna, considered the presiding deity of the city. It houses a Bhairav (Shiva) idol.
highlight: The history of Patna (Pataliputra) tied to this temple.

name: Chhoti Patan Devi
story: Located near the Badi Patan Devi, this temple is where Sati's clothes (Pat) are believed to have fallen. It has an active Shiva shrine.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: Less crowded than Badi Patan Devi.

name: Mundeshwari Devi Temple
story: Considered the oldest functional Hindu temple in the world, dating back to 108 AD. It is dedicated to Shiva (Mandaleshwar) and Shakti (Mundeshwari).
highlight: The unique octagonal plan and the Chaturmukha Shivlinga.

moreDetails.history: Built in 108 AD (Saka era) as per inscriptions.

name: Kapileshwar Sthan
story: Believed to be the hermitage of Sage Kapila, who established the Shiva Lingam here. It is a major center of faith in Mithila.
highlight: The large temple pond and the connection to Sage Kapila.

name: Maniyar Math
story: A mysterious cylindrical temple dedicated to Naga (Snake) worship, often associated with Shiva. It dates back to the Mauryan/Gupta period.
highlight: The unique cylindrical shape and ancient stucco figures.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: One of the most unique structures in Rajgir.

name: Rajnagar Shiva Temple
story: Located inside the Rajnagar Palace complex built by Maharaja Rameshwar Singh. The temple survived the 1934 earthquake which destroyed much of the palace.
highlight: The association with the Raj Darbhanga and the palace ruins.

moreDetails.history: Built by Maharaja Rameshwar Singh (20th Century).

name: Baidyanath Temple Kaimur
story: An ancient temple built by the Pratihar dynasty, known for its unique octagonal architecture similar to Khajuraho styles.
highlight: The intricate stone carvings and historical value.

name: Shiv Mandir Ramnagar
story: The most famous temple in Ramnagar, known for its splendid architecture and long-standing presence.
highlight: The intricate interior and outer structure.

name: Chaurasan Temple
story: Famous for the 84 steps (Chaurasi) leading to it. It is associated with King Harishchandra and Rohitashwa.
highlight: The climb of 84 steps and the view.

name: Rohtasgarh Shiva Temple
story: A historic Shiva temple located within the massive Rohtasgarh Fort complex, dating back to medieval times.
highlight: The location inside the historic fort on a hill.

name: Matsyagandha Mandir
story: A modern temple complex located near a lake (Rakt Kali). It features the 64 Yogini temple and a Shiva temple.
highlight: The beautiful architecture and the lake.

name: Madhaweshwar Nath Mahadev
story: Located in the historic Saurath Sabha Gachhi, famous for the annual gathering of Maithil Brahmins for marriage negotiations. The temple is central to this tradition.
highlight: The connection to the unique Saurath Sabha tradition.

name: Girihinda Shiv Mandir
story: Located on the Girihinda hill, this Shiva temple offers a stunning view of the surrounding town and fields.
highlight: The hilltop view and the serene temple.

name: Simaria Ghat Temple
story: Simaria Ghat is a major pilgrimage site known as the birthplace of poet Ramdhari Singh Dinkar. It hosts a Kalpvas and is considered a 'Mini Kumbh'.
highlight: The vibrant devout atmosphere at the Ghat.

name: Singheshwar Sthan
story: Associated with Sage Rishya Sringa who performed the Putrakameshti Yagna for Dasharatha. It is a major pilgrimage center in Mithila.

story: An old Shiva temple at the foot of a hill in Aamtoli, known for its Shivratri fair.
highlight: Annual Shivratri fair at the hill base.

name: Harihar Dham
story: Famous for housing a massive 65-feet tall Shiva Linga. It is a popular venue for marriages and religious gatherings.

name: Chitreshwar Temple
story: Home to one of the largest natural Shiva Lingas. Legend says the Pandavas worshipped here. It is near the Bengal-Odisha border.

name: Hirni Falls Temple
story: Situated in a dense forest, Hirni Falls is a popular spot. Small tribal shrines in the woods revere nature and Shiva.

name: Banpur Shiv Temple
story: A historic Shiva temple in Banpur with a pond nearby where pilgrims bathe before worship.
highlight: Pondside Shiva shrine with a Shivratri fair.

name: Shivgadi Temple
story: A cave temple located deep in the hills, housing a Swayambhu Shiva Linga. Access requires a short trek through scenic surroundings.

name: Surajkund Shiva Shrine
story: Famous for its hot water springs. The complex has shrines for various deities including Shiva, frequented by people seeking cures.

name: Pahadi Mandir (Barwadih)
story: A hilltop temple dedicated to Lord Shiva and Lord Hanuman, known for its serene setting and sweeping views.

name: Basukinath Temple
story: Considered the court where Baba Baidyanath's legal proceedings are held. Pilgrimage is incomplete without visiting here.

name: Benisagar Temples
story: An archaeological site maintained by ASI, featuring ruins of ancient temples including Shiva lingas and Panchayatana style structures.

name: Ratneshwar Nath Dham
story: An ancient temple on the banks of the Sundar river, often called the 'Baba Dham' of the Godda region. It holds great local significance.
highlight: The riverside setting and ancient Linga.

name: Belkupi Ruins
story: An ancient site with ruins of temples that show a mix of Jain and Hindu influences, including Shiva lingas.

name: Ram Mandir Shiva Shrine
story: Located in Sector 1, this is one of the oldest and most visited temples in Bokaro. The Shiva shrine here attracts huge crowds on Mondays.

name: Shiv Mandir Sector 4
story: Part of the Jagannath Temple complex in Sector 4, this Shiva temple is a major spiritual hub for the residents of the steel city.

name: Chandil Ancient Temple
story: The construction of Chandil dam submerged many ancient temples. Artifacts and Shiva lingas have been preserved in a museum nearby.

name: Bichkiliya Falls Temple
story: Located on the banks of Niranjana river, this site is a popular picnic spot with a waterfall and a temple for nature worship.

name: Chilka Dham
story: A Shiva dham near the Jharkhand-West Bengal border that draws large crowds during Shravan Somvar.

name: Sureshwar Mahadev Temple
story: A modern 108-foot-high Shivling-shaped temple in Chutia, built over a decade and consecrated in 2022.

moreDetails.history: Construction took about 10 years; consecration in 2022.

name: Baidyanath Jyotirlinga
story: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas, where Ravana sacrificed his ten heads to Shiva. It is also a Shakti Peeth where Sati's heart fell.
highlight: The Shravani Mela and the Kanwar Yatra.

name: Nandan Pahar Temple
story: A hill dedicated to Nandi, Shiva's vehicle. It has temples for Shiva, Parvati, and Nandi, and offers a view of the Baidyanath temple.
highlight: The Nandi temple and city view.

name: Tapovan Temple
story: A site of ancient penance (Tapasya) with caves and a Shiva temple (Taponath Mahadev). Legend says Sage Valmiki meditated here.
highlight: The caves and the serene atmosphere.

name: Trikut Pahar Temple
story: Located on Trikut Hill, this temple marks the spot where Ravana is said to have landed. It offers trekking and ropeway rides.
highlight: The ropeway ride and panoramic views.

name: Amadubi Village Temple
story: A rural tourism village famous for Pyatkar paintings. The village temple is a center of local life and art.

name: Bhatinda Fall Temple
story: A small Shiva shrine nestled near the Bhatinda (Moonidih) waterfall, offering a serene spot for nature lovers and devotees.

name: Shiv Shani Mandir (Dhori)
story: A notable shrine where Lord Shiva and Lord Shani are worshipped together in the Bermo area.

moreDetails.history: Established in 1975; Shani shrine added later.

name: Sukhaldari Falls Shrine
story: Located on the Kanhar river, this waterfall is stunning. Local shrines celebrate the river's power, including Shiva worship.

name: Tooti Jharna Temple
story: A mysterious temple where water from a hill naturally falls onto the Shiva Linga 24/7 throughout the year. The source of water remains unknown.

name: Tanginath Dham
story: Famous for the ancient rust-proof iron trident (Trishul) associated with Sage Parashurama. It is an archaeological site with many Shivlingas.

name: Guruhe Pahari
story: A hill temple in Garhwa offering scenic views and a challenging trek. The Shiva temple at the top is a reward for the climb.

name: Kalyanpur Shiva
story: A local Shiva temple in Kalyanpur, serving the daily spiritual needs of the residents. It is known for its peaceful ambiance.

name: Dewaki Dham
story: A famous Shiva temple where a large Shravani Mela is organized. Devotees fetch water from the river to offer here.

name: Balbal Duari
story: A famous hot spring site. A Shiva temple here is the center of the annual Balbal Mela, where people come to bathe and pray.

name: Jharkhand Dham
story: A unique roofless temple dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is one of the most significant pilgrimage sites in Giridih.

name: Khandoli Temple
story: Located near the Khandoli dam and hill, this Shiva temple attracts tourists who come for water sports and bird watching.

name: Usri Falls Temple
story: A small Shiva shrine near the scenic Usri Falls. The sound of the waterfall complements the tranquility of the temple.

name: Ratneshwar Dham
story: A major Shiva dham in Shivpur mohalla of Godda town, known for its many Shivalingas and Sawan pilgrimage.
highlight: Kanwariyas bring holy water during Shravan.

name: Mahadevshal Temple
story: Located deep in the Saranda forest, this temple was once on the railway track. The track was diverted to save the temple.
highlight: The legend of the diverted railway line.

name: Luguburu Ghantabari
story: A supreme pilgrimage site for the Santhal community. Lugu Baba is revered here, often identified with Lord Shiva in syncretic traditions.

name: Mahadev Kona
story: A scenic spot where Lord Shiva is worshipped amidst natural rock formations. It is a quiet getaway for locals.

name: Haldipokhar Shiva Mandir
story: A prominent Shiva temple in the Haldipokhar region, serving as a spiritual anchor for the local trading community.

name: Budhwa Mahadev
story: An ancient 500-year-old temple in the heart of Hazaribagh. Legend says the Linga appeared on its own. It is a major local landmark.

name: Canary Hill Temple
story: A famous landmark in Hazaribagh with a watchtower and a park. A small temple invites offering amidst the nature walk.

name: Itkhori Sahasralinga
story: Located in the Bhadrakali temple complex, this monolithic black stone Linga has 1008 miniature Lingas carved on it.

name: Chandaneswar Shiv Temple (Jamshedpur)
story: A prominent local Shiva temple in Jamshedpur that sees large Shravan Somvar gatherings.

name: Dalma Shiva Temple
story: Situated atop the Dalma hills within a wildlife sanctuary, this ancient Shiva temple is a favorite for trekkers and devotees.
highlight: The trek through the elephant sanctuary.

name: Dimna Lake Temple
story: At the foot of Dalma hills, Dimna Lake is a reservoir with scenic beauty. Small shrines dot the area for the spiritual tourist.

name: Parvat Vihar Temple

moreDetails.puranicView: Mangalnath is regarded as the birthplace of Mars (Mangal) according to the Matsya Purana, and the shrine is dedicated to Shiva on the banks of the Shipra. The site was once noted for a clear view of the planet, giving it an astronomical dimension in local sacred geography.

name: Ballaleshwar Temple (Un)
story: A mid-11th-century Shiva temple in Un notable for its later dome-like superstructure.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Heritage site with later repairs and uneven floors.

moreDetails.history: The Ballaleshwar temple is a mid 11th-century Shiva temple in Un village, notable for its dome-like superstructure added in later repairs.
moreDetails.architecture: It faces east with a square inner plan and an outer pancharatha plan; the original mandapa is lost and the garbhagriha sits below ground level.
moreDetails.darshan: The sanctum holds a svambhu-style jaladhari without a Shiva linga.
moreDetails.seasonal: Best visited in cooler months for long heritage walks.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Look for later masonry repairs and reused stonework.

name: Mahakaleshwar Temple 1 (Un)
story: A late 11th-century Shaiva temple in the Un cluster with large mandapa ruins.
highlight: Jagati platform and twin trabeate arches.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Heritage ruins with uneven stone surfaces.

moreDetails.history: Mahakaleshwar temple 1 is a late 11th-century Shiva temple in Un village, located near Chaubara Dera 1 in the Khargone district.
moreDetails.architecture: The temple faces east, stands on a jagati, and retains a damaged mandapa and shikhara with two trabeate arches between the mandapa and sanctum.
moreDetails.darshan: The sanctum and mandapa remains form the core of the heritage darshan.
moreDetails.seasonal: Cool-season visits are most comfortable for long heritage walks.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Plan for uneven stone steps and ruined sections.

name: Mahakaleshwar Temple 2 (Un)
story: An older mid-11th-century Shiva temple in Un, retaining parts of its antarala and shikhara.
highlight: Trabeate arch and surviving outer-wall carvings.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.

moreDetails.history: Mahakaleshwar temple 2 is a mid 11th-century Shiva temple in Un village, east of Jain Chaubara Dera 2 and older than Mahakaleshwar temple 1.
moreDetails.architecture: The mandapa is lost, while the antarala and part of the shikhara survive along with a trabeate arch and mutilated outer-wall artwork.
moreDetails.darshan: The surviving sanctum and architectural fragments form the heritage darshan.
moreDetails.seasonal: Dry months are best for walking the Un temple cluster.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Expect broken masonry and exposed structures.

name: Nilkantheshvara Temple (Un)
story: A late-11th-century Shaiva monument in Un with surviving sanctum doorway and carved panels.
highlight: Standing pillar from the lost mandapa.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.

moreDetails.history: The Nilkantheshvara temple of Un is a late 11th-century Shiva temple in the middle of Un village, with the mandapa largely lost.
moreDetails.architecture: A portion of the antarala and the original sanctum doorway survive, along with parts of the shikhara and outer sanctum sculptures.
moreDetails.darshan: A Shiva linga remains in the surviving sanctum.
moreDetails.seasonal: Open year-round with the best light in the morning.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: A lone pillar from the original mandapa stands nearby.

name: Bijasan Mata (Vidisha)
story: Located on a hillock; offers views of Vidisha town.

name: Jalpa Devi (Vidisha)
story: Situated on the banks of Betwa river; popular local shrine.

name: Udayagiri Cave 4 (Shiva Shrine)
story: Cave 4 at Udayagiri is noted for its Shaiva affiliation and is among the important early historical rock-cut sacred spaces in Vidisha.
highlight: Early Shaiva cave shrine context from Gupta-era Udayagiri.
entryNotes: Monument-site rules apply; check ASI timings.

moreDetails.history: The Udayagiri cave complex near Vidisha includes caves with major Vaishnava and Shaiva iconography from the Gupta period.
moreDetails.architecture: Rock-cut cave architecture with sculptural panels and early shrine spaces.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Best explored with a guide for iconographic context.

name: Udayagiri Cave 6 (Sanakanika Shiva Shrine)
story: Udayagiri Cave 6 preserves early sculptural and inscriptional evidence connected with regional rulers and Shaiva sacred activity.
highlight: Important Gupta-period cave with Shaiva association.
entryNotes: Part of the Udayagiri archaeological circuit.

moreDetails.history: Cave 6 at Udayagiri is associated with early 5th-century inscriptions and the sacred cave landscape around Vidisha.
moreDetails.architecture: Rock-cut chamber with historic sculptural context.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Combine visit with nearby Sanchi and Vidisha sites.

name: Sharda Devi (Vijayraghavgarh)
story: Located within the historic Vijayraghavgarh Fort; considered a sister shrine to Maihar.

name: Kankeshwar Temple
story: A hilltop Shiva temple near Alibaug, accessible by climbing ~700 steps, offering panoramic views of the sea.
highlight: The trek and the 'Pushkarni' tank on top.

moreDetails.history: Built by the Shilahara dynasty (9th century).

name: Sakaleshwar Temple
story: Also known as Barakhambi (12 pillars), this 13th-century temple features intricate carvings of Shiva, Saptamatrikas, and Ganesha.
highlight: The open mandapa with 12 beautifully carved pillars.

moreDetails.history: Built in 1228 AD by Yadava general Kholeshwar.

name: Shiv Mandir, Ambarnath
story: An 11th-century Shilahara temple known for its sunken, open-to-sky sanctum and ornate stone carving.
highlight: Subterranean garbhagriha and sculpted stone panels.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Expect large crowds during Mahashivratri fair days.

moreDetails.history: The Ambarnath Shiva temple was built in 1060 CE by the Shilahara dynasty and is among Maharashtra's most important medieval shrines.
moreDetails.architecture: Bhumija-style temple with a sunken sanctum and an incomplete open-to-sky shikhara.
moreDetails.darshan: The sanctum is reached by steps leading down into the main garbhagriha.
moreDetails.seasonal: Mahashivratri brings a multi-day pilgrimage fair.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Plan early visits during festival periods for easier darshan.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is the key annual celebration.

name: Anwa Temple
story: A hidden gem near the Ajanta caves, this temple is famous for its exquisitely carved pillars and ceiling.
highlight: Intricate stone carvings on pillars and the dome.
entryNotes: Located in a small village; ask locals for directions.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: A must-stop for art lovers visiting Ajanta.

name: Aundha Nagnath Temple
story: An ancient jyotirlinga shrine in Hingoli famed for Hemadpanti stonework and deep-rooted traditions.
highlight: Below-ground garbhagriha and carved stone detailing.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.

moreDetails.history: Aundha Nagnath is revered as a jyotirlinga temple in Hingoli, with traditions linked to the Yadava and Maratha periods.
moreDetails.architecture: Hemadpanti-style stonework with later Maratha-era additions defines the temple form.
moreDetails.darshan: The sanctum is set below ground level, accessed by steps.
moreDetails.seasonal: Mahashivratri brings the largest pilgrim gatherings.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Plan early entry during festival weeks for smoother access.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is the key annual celebration.

name: Balsane Temples
story: A group of 11th-century temples, with the main Shiva temple being a fine example of Bhumija style architecture.
highlight: The exquisite entrance arch and carvings.

name: Kankaleshwar Temple
story: A stunning 1000-year-old Shiva temple standing in the middle of a lake (Kankaleshwar Talav), resembling the Golden Temple of Amritsar in its setting.
highlight: The temple is surrounded by water on all sides.

moreDetails.history: Built by the Chalukya king Vikramaditya VI.

name: Bhimashankar Temple
story: A forested jyotirlinga shrine in the Sahyadris, revered as the source region of the Bhima River.
highlight: Nagara-style sanctum and the Portuguese bell in the temple complex.
bestTime: Monsoon greenery and cool winter mornings.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Monsoon weekends can be crowded; expect forest sanctuary checks.

moreDetails.history: One of the twelve jyotirlingas, Bhimashankar has been a pilgrimage center for centuries, with later additions including a temple hall associated with the Peshwa era.
moreDetails.architecture: Nagara-style temple architecture with later Maratha-period additions in the mandapa.
moreDetails.darshan: The sanctum enshrines the jyotirlinga, with a heritage bell visible within the complex.
moreDetails.seasonal: Shravan and Mahashivratri bring peak pilgrim traffic.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: The temple sits within the Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary; plan travel accordingly.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri and Shravan month rituals draw major crowds.

name: Markanda Mahadev Temple
story: Known as the 'Khajuraho of Vidarbha', this temple complex is famous for its intricate erotic carvings and riverbank setting.
highlight: Exquisite stone carvings resembling Khajuraho temples.

moreDetails.history: Attributed to the Rashtrakuta dynasty (8th-12th century), revived by the Gond kings.
moreDetails.architecture: Nagara style with rich sculptural bands.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: A must for art history lovers.

name: Changdev Maharaj Temple
story: Dedicated to the yogi Changdev who lived for 1400 years; located at the confluence of Purna and Tapi rivers.

name: Rameshwar Temple (Chaul)
story: An ancient temple in the historic town of Chaul, featuring a massive built-up tank (Pokharan) and Hemadpanti architecture.
highlight: The large temple tank (Pokharan) and the peaceful courtyard.

moreDetails.history: Chaul was a major port; the temple reflects its prosperity.

name: Kunkeshwar Temple
story: A stunning Shiva temple located right on the Arabian Sea beach, often called the 'Kashi of Konkan'.

moreDetails.history: Built by the Yadavas in the 12th century; Shivaji Maharaj visited frequently.

name: Dharmapuri Kedarnath
story: A grand temple dedicated to Kedarnath, located within a mud fort. It is known for its intricate Chalukyan carvings.

moreDetails.history: Built by Chalukya king Vikramaditya VI.

name: Kailasa Temple, Ellora
story: A monumental monolithic Shiva temple carved from rock at Ellora's Cave 16.
highlight: Vast rock-cut courtyards and sculpted panels.
bestTime: Morning heritage walks and winter weather.
timings: Heritage site hours; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Part of the Ellora heritage complex; plan for additional cave visits.

moreDetails.history: Commissioned during the Rashtrakuta era, the Kailasa Temple is the largest rock-cut Hindu temple at Ellora.
moreDetails.architecture: Carved from a single rock mass with elaborate sculptural treatments and multi-level courts.
moreDetails.darshan: The shrine is approached through monumental rock-cut gateways and courtyards.
moreDetails.seasonal: Winter and early morning visits are most comfortable.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Ellora has multiple cave groups; allow extra time for exploration.
moreDetails.festivals: Primarily a heritage destination rather than a festival site.

name: Kailash Temple (Ellora)
story: Cave 16 of Ellora, carved from a single rock from top to bottom. It is considered one of the most remarkable cave temples in the world.
highlight: The largest monolithic rock-cut structure in the world.

moreDetails.history: Built by Rashtrakuta King Krishna I in the 8th century.

name: Elephanta Caves
story: Famous for the colossal 'Maheshmurti' (Sadashiva) sculpture representing the three aspects of Shiva: Creator, Preserver, and Destroyer.
entryNotes: Requires a ferry ride from Gateway of India.

moreDetails.history: Dated to the 5th-7th centuries; attributed to Kalachuris or Konkan Mauryas.

name: Vyadeshwar Temple
story: A prominent Shiva temple in the coastal town of Guhagar, believed to be the Kuldaivat (family deity) of many Chitpavan Brahmin families.
highlight: Traditional Konkani architecture and proximity to Guhagar beach.

moreDetails.history: Ancient origins; renovated in modern times. Legends link it to Parashurama.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Visit the pristine Guhagar beach nearby.
moreDetails.festivals: Tripuri Purnima is celebrated with deepotsav.

name: Harihareshwar Temple
story: Known as 'Dakshin Kashi', this temple is unique for its Pradakshina (circumambulation) path that goes around the hill and along the sea rocks.
highlight: The scenic and adventurous Pradakshina path along the sea.
bestTime: Winter; avoid Pradakshina during high tide/monsoon.
entryNotes: Check tide timings before doing the rock pradakshina.

moreDetails.history: Ancient pilgrimage site revered by Peshwas.
moreDetails.architecture: Konkani style with Kalbhairav shrine nearby.
moreDetails.seasonal: Monsoon is dangerous for the sea path.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Start with Kalbhairav darshan as per tradition.

name: Kedareshwar Cave Temple
story: A cave shrine on Harishchandragad where the Shiva linga is surrounded by water.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: The cave often has water on the floor; plan accordingly.

moreDetails.history: Kedareshwar Cave is a noted Shiva shrine on Harishchandragad, approached via a trek.
moreDetails.architecture: Natural cave shrine with a central linga and carved niches.
moreDetails.darshan: The linga is surrounded by water, requiring wading for closer access.
moreDetails.seasonal: Water levels rise during monsoon; post-monsoon is preferred.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Carry trekking essentials and plan for wet cave floors.

name: Ramling (Hatkanangale)
story: An ancient cave temple dedicated to Shiva, carved into the Ramling hill. Legend says Rama worshipped Shiva here.

name: Hottal Siddheshwar
