story: A masterpiece of Chalukyan architecture, this temple was dismantled and completely restored by the archaeology department.
highlight: The incredible restoration work and sculpture.

name: Adasa
story: Adasa is a Shiva temple in Maharashtra with active local worship traditions.
bestTime: October to March and Mahashivratri period.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Footwear is not allowed inside temple areas.

name: Khandoba Temple (Jejuri)
story: The 'Golden Temple' of Maharashtra, where devotees shower turmeric (Bhandara) on each other, turning the whole hill yellow.
dressCode: Modest; expect to get covered in yellow powder.
entryNotes: Be prepared for the turmeric dust.

moreDetails.history: Historic hill fort temple dedicated to Khandoba, a warrior avatar of Shiva.
moreDetails.seasonal: Festival days are crowded but unique.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Protect camera gear from turmeric dust.

name: Kukdeshwar Temple
story: A scenic 12th-century ruined temple situated on the banks of the Kukadi river, featuring elaborate stone carvings.
highlight: The intricate roof carvings and the peaceful riverside ruins.

moreDetails.history: Built by the Shilahara dynasty; now a protected monument.

name: Khidkaleshwar Temple
story: An ancient temple located near the Khidkali lake, believed to have been visited by the Pandavas during their exile.
highlight: The serene lake and old stone structure.

name: Kopeshwar Temple
story: A Shilahara-era Shiva temple on the Krishna River, celebrated for its sculptural mandapas.
highlight: Carved stone pillars and riverfront precincts.
bestTime: Morning light on the stone carvings.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Footwear is not allowed inside temple areas.

moreDetails.history: Kopeshwar Temple is an 11th-12th century Shaiva shrine built by the Shilahara rulers at Khidrapur on the Krishna River.
moreDetails.architecture: Stone mandapas and sculptural pillars mark the temple, with a conical sanctum typical of the era.
moreDetails.darshan: The Shiva linga is housed in a dedicated sanctum with mandapa approach.
moreDetails.seasonal: Festival days draw higher pilgrim traffic.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Khidrapur lies between Kolhapur and Sangli; plan transport accordingly.

name: Bhairavnath Temple (Kikali)
story: A hidden masterpiece of the Yadava era, known for its incredible hexagonal mandapa and intricate sculptures of deities.
highlight: The hexagonal Sabhamandapa and the hero stones outside.

name: Unkeshwar Temple
story: Famous for natural hot water springs containing sulfur, believed to cure skin diseases, located near a Shiva temple.

name: Jyotiba Temple
story: A major pilgrimage site near Kolhapur dedicated to Jyotiba (an incarnation of Shiva), where devotees scatter pink 'Gulal' powder.
highlight: The pink-colored temple complex due to Gulal.
entryNotes: Located on a hill; drive or climb available.

moreDetails.history: Jyotiba helped Mahalaxmi to kill demons; temple built by Scindias.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Combine with Mahalaxmi temple in Kolhapur.

name: Anandeshwar Temple
story: A lesser-known gem in Vidarbha, this temple is built like a fort using massive black stones and features a unique three-shrine layout.
highlight: Massive black stone masonry and fort-like appearance.
entryNotes: Located on the banks of Purna river.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: Rare example of this style in the region.

name: Gomukh Temple (Lonar)
story: Situated on the rim of the famous Lonar Meteor crater, this temple has a perennial stream (Dhara) that flows into the holy tank.
highlight: The eternal water stream and the view of the crater lake.
entryNotes: Requires walking down steps into the crater rim area.

moreDetails.history: Ancient temple built around the crater's fresh water source.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Do not miss the Daitya Sudan temple in town.

name: Mahabaleshwar Temple (Old)
story: The ancient temple in Old Mahabaleshwar, considered the source of five holy rivers (Krishna, Venna, Koyna, Savitri, Gayatri).
entryNotes: Located 6km from the main hill station market.

moreDetails.history: Built by the Yadava kings in the 13th century.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Visit the Krishnabai temple nearby for a view.

name: Siddhanath Temple, Mhaswad
story: A 9th-century shrine honoring Siddhanath (Shiva) with a famed chariot festival in Mhaswad.
highlight: Annual Rath Yatra and riverside setting.
bestTime: Rath Yatra season and winter visits.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Festival days feature large processions and fairs.

moreDetails.history: Siddhanath Temple in Mhaswad dates to early medieval times and honors Siddhanath, an incarnation of Shiva.
moreDetails.architecture: Stone temple with a long-standing tradition of annual fairs.
moreDetails.darshan: The sanctum enshrines Siddhanath with supporting shrines nearby.
moreDetails.seasonal: The Rath Yatra fair draws the largest gatherings.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Expect heavy crowds and market stalls during the yatra.
moreDetails.festivals: The annual Siddhanath Rath Yatra is the main celebration.

name: Nagnath Temple (Mohol)
story: A major Shiva temple in the Solapur region, famous for its grand annual procession (Palkhi).
highlight: The temple architecture and the vibrant Palkhi festival.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: A key center for local culture.

name: Babulnath Temple
story: A hilltop Shiva temple in Girgaum, among Mumbai's oldest places of worship.
highlight: Steps to the hillock shrine near Chowpatty.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Expect stair climbs and city traffic near Girgaum.

moreDetails.history: Babulnath is dedicated to Shiva as the Lord of the Babul tree and is among Mumbai's oldest temples.
moreDetails.architecture: Hilltop shrine with a stepped approach and city-facing courtyard.
moreDetails.darshan: The main sanctum houses the Shiva linga with daily rituals.
moreDetails.seasonal: Mahashivratri and Diwali bring the biggest crowds.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Plan visits during off-peak hours for easier access.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri and Diwali are key celebrations.

name: Jabreshwar Mahadev Mandir
story: A Nagara-style Shiva temple near Banganga tank in Walkeshwar, Malabar Hill.
highlight: Banganga precinct and Malabar Hill heritage walks.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Temple sits near Banganga tank; expect narrow lanes.

moreDetails.history: Jabreshwar Mahadev Mandir was built in the 19th century and is part of the Walkeshwar-Banganga heritage area.
moreDetails.architecture: North Indian Nagara-style shikhara over the sanctum.
moreDetails.darshan: The sanctum houses the Shiva linga, with Banganga tank nearby.
moreDetails.seasonal: Evening visits are popular during cooler months.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Combine darshan with Banganga heritage walk.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is observed with special pujas.

name: Jogeshwari Caves
story: One of the earliest Hindu cave temples in India (dating back to 520-550 CE), located in the suburbs of Mumbai.
highlight: Ancient carvings hidden in a dense urban jungle.

moreDetails.history: Built by Pashupata sect monks in the 6th century.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Surrounded by slums but historically vital.

name: Mandapeshwar Caves
story: A rock-cut Shiva temple that was converted into a church by the Portuguese and later reclaimed. It sits just below a Portuguese monastery ruins.
highlight: The Nataraja carving and the history of religious conversion.

name: Walkeshwar Temple
story: Located at the highest point of Mumbai city, legend says Lord Rama created a Linga from sand (Valuka-Ishwar) here.
highlight: The ancient Banganga tank adjacent to the temple.
entryNotes: Parking is difficult in Malabar Hill.

moreDetails.history: Original temple built by Shilaharas; destroyed by Portuguese and rebuilt.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Walk around the Banganga tank for a timeless feel.
moreDetails.festivals: Music festival is a cultural treat.

name: Baneshwar Temple
story: A temple built by the Peshwas located in a dense forest area with a waterfall, often used as a picnic spot.

moreDetails.history: Built by Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao.

name: Kapaleshwar Temple
story: A unique Shiva temple where there is no Nandi statue facing the Linga, as Nandi is considered a Guru here.
entryNotes: Located in the busy Panchavati area.

moreDetails.history: Mythology says Shiva was cleansed of Brahma-hatya sin here.

name: Naroshankar Temple
story: Famous for the massive 'Naroshankar Bell' (looted from the Portuguese at Vasai Fort) and its fortress-like walls on the Godavari bank.
highlight: The historic Portuguese church bell installed in a Hindu temple.

name: Someshwar Temple
story: A popular Shiva temple on the banks of the Godavari, known for its pleasant climate and boating facilities.
highlight: Riverside location and Dudhsagar waterfall nearby.

name: Parli Vaijnath Temple
story: A Marathwada jyotirlinga shrine known for its hilltop setting and Ahilyabai Holkar-era renovations.
highlight: Brass-plated gates and the sacred Parli corridor.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Footwear is not allowed inside temple areas.

moreDetails.history: Parli Vaijnath is a jyotirlinga temple in Beed district, with major renovations credited to Ahilyabai Holkar.
moreDetails.architecture: Stone temple complex with a raised approach and fortified walls typical of Maratha-era renovations.
moreDetails.darshan: The jyotirlinga sanctum is the focal point of the complex rituals.
moreDetails.seasonal: Shravan and Mahashivratri periods are the busiest.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Local queues and temple trust arrangements operate during peak festivals.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is the largest annual event.

name: Jabareshwar Temple
story: A beautiful Hemadpanti temple in Phaltan, known for its intricate Nandi mandapa and artistic pillars.
highlight: The stone carvings typical of the era.

name: Prakasha Kedareshwar
story: Known as 'Dakshin Kashi' of the tribal belt, this temple is an important pilgrimage site on the banks of the Tapi river.

moreDetails.history: One of the oldest temples in Khandesh.

name: Nilkantheshwar (Pune)
story: A hilltop temple offering panoramic views of the Panshet and Varasgaon dams, built recently but popular for its location.
highlight: The breathtaking view of the backwaters.

name: Omkareshwar Temple, Pune
story: A Peshwa-era Shiva temple on the Mutha river with a distinctive multi-domed roof.
highlight: Nine-domed courtyard and riverfront heritage setting.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Temple sits on the Mutha riverbank; plan for local traffic.

moreDetails.history: Built during the Peshwa period, the temple is a heritage landmark on the Mutha river in Shaniwar Peth.
moreDetails.architecture: The complex features a courtyard with multiple domes and a prominent Nandi shrine.
moreDetails.darshan: The Shiva linga sits in the main sanctum with a mandapa approach.
moreDetails.seasonal: Shravan Somvar and Mahashivratri bring the highest crowds.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Evening aarti draws local devotees; arrive early in festival weeks.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri and Shravan Mondays are the main observances.

name: Pataleshwar Caves
story: An 8th-century rock-cut Shaiva cave temple with a circular Nandi mandapa.
highlight: Monolithic mandapa and historic cave sanctums.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Heritage monument rules apply; avoid peak afternoon heat.

moreDetails.history: Pataleshwar is a Rashtrakuta-era rock-cut Shiva temple in Pune and is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India.
moreDetails.architecture: Monolithic excavation with a circular Nandi mandapa and pillared hall.
moreDetails.darshan: The central sanctum houses a Shiva linga, with side shrines within the cave.
moreDetails.seasonal: Winter visits are most comfortable for heritage walks.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: The caves are in central Pune; arrive early for quieter darshan.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is the key annual observance.

name: Jagadishwar Temple
story: The personal temple of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj located on Raigad Fort, near his Samadhi.
highlight: Historical connection to the Maratha empire.
entryNotes: Requires ropeway or trek to the fort.

moreDetails.architecture: Unique dome that resembles Islamic style (communal harmony).
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Pay respects at the Samadhi nearby.

name: Dhutpapeshwar Temple
story: A scenic temple situated on the banks of the Mrudani river with a beautiful waterfall cascading near the temple premises.
entryNotes: Located in a valley; scenic drive.

moreDetails.history: Ancient site; the name implies 'Washer of Sins'.

name: Amruteshwar Temple
story: An intricately carved Shilahara-era Shiva temple in the Bhandardara region.
highlight: Stone carving details and village approach.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Rural approach roads; plan transport in advance.

moreDetails.history: Built in the 9th century by the Shilahara dynasty, Amruteshwar is a key Shiva temple at Ratanwadi.
moreDetails.architecture: Hemadpanti-style stone construction with intricate carvings.
moreDetails.darshan: The sanctum houses the Shiva linga and a historic mandapa approach.
moreDetails.seasonal: Mahashivratri brings increased local pilgrim visits.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Combine visits with Bhandardara region excursions.

name: Suvarneshwar Temple
story: A serene temple in Ratnagiri known for its clean architecture and peaceful surroundings.

name: Karneshwar Temple
story: Attributed to Karna from the Mahabharata, this temple is a fine example of ancient architecture in the Konkan region.

moreDetails.history: Built by the Chalukyas/Yadavas; Sambhaji Maharaj was captured nearby.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Visit the Sambhaji Maharaj memorial nearby.

name: Marleshwar Temple
story: A cave temple famous for the Dhareshwar waterfall and the belief that cobras in the cave do not harm devotees.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: Beware of slippery paths in monsoon.

name: Sangameshwar Temple (Saswad)
story: Located at the confluence of the Karha and Chamli rivers, this temple is a masterpiece of Yadava-era architecture.
highlight: The confluence (Sangam) setting and the Nandi mandapa.
entryNotes: On the river bank; easy access.

moreDetails.history: Built during the Yadava period; associated with the Peshwas later.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Visit the Samadhi of Sopan Maharaj nearby.

name: Pateshwar Shiva Temple
story: A quiet hill temple complex known for thousands of miniature Shiva lingas carved into the rocks.
entryNotes: Requires a drive up the hill.

name: Sangameshwar (Mahuli)
story: Located at the confluence of Krishna and Venna rivers, this temple complex (Sangameshwar and Vishveshwar) is a gem of Maratha architecture.
highlight: The grand river confluence and the deepmalas.

name: Shikhar Shingnapur
story: A major hilltop temple dedicated to Shambhu Mahadev, considered the family deity (Kuldaivat) of many Marathi families.
highlight: The tough trek to the top and the 'Kawad' procession.
entryNotes: Located on a high hill peak.

moreDetails.seasonal: Summer fair is very hot but popular.

name: Gondeshwar Temple
story: An 11th-12th century Bhumija Shiva temple with a panchayatana complex in Sinnar.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Heritage monument rules apply; check local timings.

moreDetails.history: Gondeshwar Temple dates to the Yadava period and is a protected monument in Sinnar.
moreDetails.architecture: Bhumija-style panchayatana plan with a main Shiva shrine and four subsidiary shrines.
moreDetails.darshan: The main sanctum houses the Shiva linga, with subsidiary shrines around.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Combine with nearby heritage temples in Nashik district.

name: Hattarsang Kudal
story: A magnificent temple located at the confluence of the Bhima and Sina rivers, known for its inscriptions and preservation.
highlight: The Harihareshwar temple at the river confluence.

name: Siddheshwar Temple
story: A Lingayat shrine around Siddheshwar Lake, honoring Siddheshwar and the local Shiva tradition.
highlight: Temple-lake complex and the Gadda Yatra fair.
bestTime: Makar Sankranti celebrations and winter evenings.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Festival periods can be crowded; expect processions.

moreDetails.history: The temple honors Siddheshwar, a devotee of Shiva revered in the Lingayat tradition, with a lake-centered complex in Solapur.
moreDetails.architecture: Large temple complex with multiple shrines around the lake.
moreDetails.darshan: The main shrine is complemented by smaller temples within the complex.
moreDetails.seasonal: Makar Sankranti and Gadda Yatra bring the biggest crowds.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Plan around festival routes during the annual yatra.
moreDetails.festivals: Makar Sankranti and the Gadda Yatra are the key festivals.

name: Uttareshwar Temple (Ter)
story: One of the oldest surviving brick temples in Maharashtra, dating back to the Vakataka/Gupta period (4th-6th century).
highlight: Rare ancient brick architecture and carved wooden doorframes.

moreDetails.history: Ter was a major trade center (Tagara); the temple is a survivor from that era.
moreDetails.architecture: Brick construction with stupa-like roof (Wagora style).

name: Kopineshwar Mandir
story: Thane's patron Shiva temple known for one of the largest lingas in Maharashtra.
highlight: Prominent linga and temple complex near Masunda Lake.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Expect local market crowds around the temple lanes.

moreDetails.history: Built by the Shilahara dynasty, Kopineshwar has undergone multiple renovations since the 18th century.
moreDetails.architecture: Traditional temple complex with a large central linga and multiple shrines.
moreDetails.darshan: The main sanctum houses the large Shiva linga revered by Thane devotees.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Two entry gates serve the complex; plan based on crowd flow.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is the most visited festival.

name: Trimbakeshwar Shiva Temple
story: A jyotirlinga shrine in Trimbak where the Godavari begins and the three-faced linga represents the Trimurti.
highlight: Three-faced linga and the Brahmagiri pilgrim circuit.
bestTime: Early morning; Shravan Mondays for devotional ambience.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Expect queues during Shravan and Mahashivratri.

moreDetails.history: An ancient jyotirlinga shrine at Trimbak, rebuilt in stone during the Peshwa era, with a linga that represents Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.
moreDetails.architecture: Hemadpanthi-style stone architecture with a prominent courtyard and carved shikhara.
moreDetails.darshan: The sanctum enshrines the three-faced jyotirlinga, with the Godavari source nearby at Brahmagiri.
moreDetails.seasonal: Shravan Somvars and Mahashivratri draw the highest crowds.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Plan early entries during peak seasons for smoother darshan.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri and Shravan Somvar rituals are the major highlights.

name: Tungareshwar Temple
story: A popular Shiva temple located deep inside the Tungareshwar Wildlife Sanctuary, accessible via a trek or dirt road.
highlight: Location inside a dense forest sanctuary.
entryNotes: Entry fees for sanctuary apply; roads are rough.

moreDetails.history: Dedicated to Lord Tungareshwar; popular with Mumbai trekkers.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Leopards are present in the sanctuary; be careful.
moreDetails.festivals: Huge crowds of walkers in Shravan.

name: Velneshwar Temple
story: A serene coastal temple dedicated to Shiva, flanked by a beautiful, clean beach.

moreDetails.history: Kuldaivat of the Gokhale family; ancient origins.

name: Grishneshwar Temple
story: A jyotirlinga shrine near Ellora, known for Hemadpanthi stonework and pilgrimage lore.
highlight: Verul village darshan with Ellora caves nearby.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Footwear is not allowed inside the sanctum area.

moreDetails.history: Grishneshwar is one of the twelve jyotirlingas and sits at Verul near the Ellora Caves in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district.
moreDetails.architecture: The temple is associated with Hemadpanthi-style stone construction common in the region.
moreDetails.darshan: The jyotirlinga sanctum is the focal point of daily rituals and pilgrim queues.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Combine darshan with Ellora heritage visits in the same trip.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is the key annual celebration.

name: Kashi Vishveshwar Temple
story: Located in Wai (Dakshin Kashi), this temple is known for its huge Nandi statue carved from a single stone.
highlight: The massive Nandi and the Krishna river ghats.

moreDetails.history: Built in 1760; synonymous with the Peshwa culture.

name: Bhuleshwar Temple
story: A hilltop Shiva temple famed for its carvings and the fort-top setting near Yawat.
highlight: Basalt carvings and panoramic fort views.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: The temple sits on a hill; expect short climbs.

moreDetails.history: Bhuleshwar Temple is an 8th-century Shiva shrine and a protected monument near Pune.
moreDetails.architecture: Basalt stone construction with classical carvings and sculpted panels.
moreDetails.darshan: The sanctum houses the Shiva linga, reached via a hilltop approach.
moreDetails.seasonal: Monsoon and winter visits are most comfortable.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Carry water for the hill climb during hot months.

name: Ramling Temple (Yedshi)
story: Located in the Ramling Ghat Wildlife Sanctuary, this temple is situated in a ravine and is associated with Lord Rama's exile.
highlight: The railway track passing nearby and the sanctuary setting.

name: Mankeshwar Temple
story: A classic example of Hemadpanti architecture located on the Mumbai-Agra highway, known for its intricate stone carvings.

moreDetails.history: Built in the 12th century by Yadava rulers.
moreDetails.architecture: Star-shaped plan typical of Hemadpanti style.
moreDetails.seasonal: Good stopover on a road trip.

name: Amareswar Temple
story: A prominent temple in the Prachi Valley; legend says Indra worshipped here.

name: Akhandalamani Temple
story: Famous for curing diseases and snake bites; situated on the banks of Baitarani river.

name: Bhattarika Temple
story: Primarily a Shakti Peetha but houses a significant Shiva shrine; on the Mahanadi banks.

name: Kosaleswar Temple
story: Located on the banks of Tel river; known for its Tantric sculptures and ruinous grandeur.

name: Harishankar Temple
story: Located on the Gandhamardan hills; dedicated to Harihara. Famous for a perennial waterfall.

name: Chandaneshwar Temple
story: Located near the Bengal border; famous for the gruesome Charak Puja (hook swinging) during Chaitra Parva.

name: Baneswar Temple
story: Believed to be established by Banasura; features a beautiful pond.

name: Charchika Temple
story: One of the eight Shakta shrines of Odisha; houses a Shiva temple in the complex.

name: Maninageswar Temple
story: An ancient temple dedicated to Maninageswar; known for its historical inscriptions.

name: Koili Ghutar
story: Known for ancient rock art and a rock-cut Shiva shrine.

name: Belkhandi Temple
story: An archaeological site at the confluence of Tel and Uttei rivers; ancient Shiva temple ruins.

name: Bhushandeswar Temple
story: Houses one of the largest Shiva Lingas in Asia (12 feet tall), carved from black granite.

name: Bhaskareswar Temple
story: Houses a massive 9ft Shiva Linga, believed by some to be a remnant of an Ashokan pillar.

name: Brahmeswara Temple
story: A panchatanaya (five-shrine) temple known for its mature Kalinga style and use of iron beams.

name: Chakreshvari Temple
story: A smaller shrine dedicated to Shiva, often associated with Chakra worship.

name: Chintamaniswar Temple
story: Located near Chintamaniswar tank; believed to fulfill wishes (Chinta-Mani).

name: Kapilesvara Temple
story: Associated with Sage Kapila; believed to be the council hall of Shiva.

name: Kedareswar Temple
story: Part of the Kedar Gouri complex; associated with the legend of lovers Kedar and Gouri.

name: Lakhesvara Temple
story: Located on the Gangeswar-Yamuneswar road; traditionally linked to the donation of a lakh coins.

name: Lingaraj Temple
story: The largest temple in Bhubaneswar, dedicated to Harihara (Shiva and Vishnu). A masterpiece of Kalinga architecture.

name: Markandeswar Temple
story: Situated near Bindusagar; famous for the Markandeya tank and cleansing rituals.

name: Megheswar Temple
story: Dedicated to the Lord of Clouds; built by Swapnesvara Deva. Known for its Saptaratha plan.

name: Mukteshvara Temple
story: Known as the 'Gem of Odisha architecture' for its exquisite carvings and unique Torana (archway).

name: Parasuramesvara Temple
story: One of the oldest existing temples in Bhubaneswar, featuring early Kalinga style and Saptamatrika carvings.

name: Rajarani Temple
story: Famous for its erotic carvings and lack of a presiding deity; built with reddish-gold sandstone (Rajarani).

name: Rameswar Temple
story: Known as the Mausi Maa temple of Lingaraj; the chariot (Rukuna Rath) comes here during Ashokashtami.

name: Sarneshwar Shiva Temple
story: An ancient Shiva temple in the Old Town area.

name: Siddheswara Temple
story: Standing within the Mukteswara complex, taller but simpler in ornamentation.

name: Sisiresvar Temple
story: Located in the Vaital Deula compound; dedicated to Shiva.

name: Talesvara Temple
story: A temple that has seen damage and restoration; name suggests association with Tala (Palm) tree.

name: Uttaresvara Temple
story: Located on the northern bank of Bindusagar tank; one of the four main temples around the tank.

name: Vaital Deula
story: A unique Khakhara-style temple dedicated to Chamunda (Shakti/Shiva Tantra). Known as Tini Mundia.

name: Yameshwar Temple
story: Dedicated to Yama (Lord of Death) who worships Shiva here. Similar to Jameshwar.

name: Papakhya Ghat Temple
story: Located on the Mahanadi bank; bathing here during eclipse is believed to wash away sins.

name: Chatikona Temple
story: Famous for the Shiva temple near the waterfall and the weekly tribal market of Dongria Kondhs.

name: Budhakhol Temple
story: A heritage site with five Shiva temples and Buddhist remnants, situated on a hill with a waterfall.

name: Chakrapada Temple
story: Dedicated to Lord Birupakshya; situated amidst nature.

name: Murga Mahadev
story: Situated near a waterfall; a popular pilgrimage spot for tribals and locals alike.

name: Mahavinayak Temple
story: A unique temple dedicated to the five deities (Shiva, Vishnu, Durga, Sun, Ganesha) in one Linga.

name: Dhabaleswar Temple
story: Located on an island in the Mahanadi river; Shiva is worshipped as 'Dhabala' (White) owing to a legend of a thief.

name: Kupeshawar Temple
story: Located near the Barabati Fort moat; an ancient temple of the fort area.

name: Kuseileswar Temple
story: Located on the bank of Kusei river; built by the Bhanja kings.

name: Pradhanpat Temple
story: Located near the Pradhanpat waterfall; adjacent to the royal palace.

name: Kapilash Temple
story: Known as the Kailash of Odisha; situated 2239 feet above sea level. Accessed by 1352 steps.

name: Charisambhu Temple
story: Famous twin temples of Nilamadhab (Vishnu) and Siddheswar (Shiva); architectural marvels.

name: Bateswar Temple
story: Ancient temple near the sea mouth (Potagada); often buried under sand dunes.

name: Singhanath Temple
story: Located on a rocky island in Mahanadi; the only temple of its kind in Odisha.

name: Bimaleswar (Huma)
story: The presiding deity of the Huma leaning temple.

name: Sidheshwar Temple
story: Located at Dasaswamedh Ghat on Baitarani river; main spot for Pinda Daan.

name: Trilochaneswar Temple
story: Part of the Biraja Kshetra; dedicated to the three-eyed Shiva.

name: Gokarneswar Temple
story: Located on the banks of Brahmani river; historically significant.

name: Gupteswar Cave Temple
story: A limestone cave temple where the Linga is growing; believed to be worshipped by Rama.

name: Dhabaleswar (Jharsuguda)
story: A prominent Shiva temple in the industrial belt; calm amidst activity.

name: Astasambhu (Kualo)
story: A cluster of eight Shiva temples with Kanakeswar as the main deity; a masterpiece of Bhaumakara art.

name: Gonasika Temple (Brahmeshwar)
story: The source of Baitarani river (Gonasika - Cow's Nostril); the temple is dedicated to Brahmeshwar Shiva.

name: Chandrashekhar Temple
story: Located in the Kichakeswari complex; a fine example of Bhanja dynasty architecture.

name: Kutaitundi Temple
story: A small but artistically significant temple in Khiching.

name: Patali Srikhetra
story: Place where Lord Jagannath was hidden underground (Patali) during invasions; houses Shiva shrines too.

name: Jogisarda Temple
story: An ancient temple dedicated to Shiva, historically associated with Jogis (ascetics).

name: Mohangiri Temple
story: A ruined temple near a stream; known for exquisite Tantric carvings.

name: Sobhaneswar Temple
story: Located on the banks of Prachi river; known for its fine workmanship.

name: Panchalingeswar Temple
story: Five Lingas submerged in a perennial stream on the Nilagiri hills; scenic beauty.

name: Balunkeswar Temple
story: A popular Shiva temple near the famous Raghunath Jew temple.

name: Nrusinghanath (Pareshwar)
story: While famous for Nrusinghanath (Vishnu), the site houses ancient Shiva lingas like Pareshwar.

name: Mahendragiri Temples
story: Located on Odisha's second highest peak; ancient temples built by Pandavas (Bhima, Kunti, Yudhishthira).

name: Swapneswar Temple
story: Located on the banks of Salunki river; deity appeared in a dream (Swapna).

name: Beleswar Temple
story: Located on the sea beach near Puri; serene atmosphere.

name: Jameshwar Temple
story: Dedicated to Jameshwar (Shiva worshiped by Yama); protects pilgrims from the God of Death.

name: Kapalamochana Temple
story: Located near Manikarnika Sahi; believed to be where Shiva was freed from the sin of cutting Brahma's head.

name: Lokanatha Temple
story: The guardian deity of Puri Jagannath Temple's treasury; the Linga remains submerged in water throughout the year except on Pankoddhar Ekadashi.

name: Markandeshwar Temple (Puri)
story: Where Sage Markandeya meditated; famous for the Markandeya tank and ancient Saptamatrika images.

name: Taratarini (Shiva Shrine)
story: A major Shakti Peetha that includes a shrine for Shiva as Tumbeswar.

name: Indralath Temple
story: One of the tallest brick temples in Odisha; originally Vaishnava but associated with the Shaiva complex.

name: Someshwar Temple (Ranipur)
story: The main Shiva temple at the famous Chausathi Yogini site; reflects Somavamsi art.

name: Pataleswar (Paikapada)
story: Famous for the assembly of 99,99,99 large and small Lingas spread across the complex.

name: Khirachora Gopinath (Shiva Shrine)
story: Famous Vaishnava temple that houses an ancient Shiva shrine within its complex.

name: Ghoghar Dham
story: Located on the banks of Ib river; naturally formed Lingas in the rocky gorge.

name: Vedvyas Temple
story: At the confluence of Sankh, Koel and Saraswati rivers; where Ved Vyas wrote the Mahabharata.

name: Huma Temple
story: The famous Leaning Temple of Huma; known for Kudo fish that are fed by devotees and never caught.

name: Ladukeswar (Sarankul)
story: Popularly known as Ladu Baba; famous for granting wishes and its playful monkeys.

name: Godhaneswar Temple
story: Dedicated to the protector of cows (Go-Dhana); situated in the temple town of Sonepur.

name: Lankeswari Temple
story: Dedicated to Goddess Lankeswari but deeply connected to Ravana's Shiva worship; situated on a river island.

name: Suvarnameru Temple
story: Situated at the confluence of Mahanadi and Tel; Sonepur is known as 'Lanka' in local legend.

name: Ulapgarh (Usakothi)
story: Ruins of an ancient fort with a Shiva temple; panoramic views.

name: Rishikesh Mahadev
story: An ancient temple located in the Aravali hills near Abu Road, believed to be thousands of years old and mentioned in scriptures.
highlight: Its antiquity and location in the valley.

moreDetails.history: Considered to be from the Vedic era; renovated by Ambrish Rishi.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: A quiet alternative to Mount Abu crowds.

name: Markandeshwar Temple
story: An ancient temple dedicated to Sage Markandeya. It is famous locally for rituals related to exorcism and healing.
highlight: The nearby Saraswati Kund and the tribal rituals.

moreDetails.history: Very old site with footprints of the sage.
moreDetails.architecture: Ancient stone pillars and small shrines.
moreDetails.festivals: Regular flow of devotees seeking cures.

name: Chamunda Mata (Ajmer)
story: Located in the hills of Ajmer; believed to be worshipped by Prithviraj Chauhan.

name: Bhartrihari Temple
story: Dedicated to the sage Bhartrihari (brother of King Vikramaditya), who renounced his kingdom to meditate here. It is a major pilgrimage site.
highlight: The eternal flame (dhuni) that has been burning for centuries.
entryNotes: On the road to Sariska; monkeys are plentiful.

moreDetails.darshan: Devotees pay respects to the Samadhi.
moreDetails.seasonal: Very crowded during the rainy season fair.
moreDetails.festivals: The annual fair is one of Alwar's biggest.

name: Naldeshwar Shrine
story: A small Shiva shrine surrounded by dense greenery and rocky hills, accessible via a short trek.
highlight: Natural waterfall (in monsoon) and rock formations.
bestTime: Monsoon (July-Sept) is the only time to see the falls.
entryNotes: Located off the Alwar-Jaipur highway; requires a walk.

moreDetails.history: A natural site worshipped for centuries by locals.
moreDetails.seasonal: Dry in summer; magical in monsoon.
moreDetails.festivals: Locals picnic here on Shiva festivals.

name: Talvriksha Mahadev
story: A scenic spot famous for its hot water springs and the temple where Sage Mandavya is believed to have performed penance.
highlight: Hot sulfur springs believed to have medicinal properties.

moreDetails.history: Ancient site associated with the Mahabharata and local sages.
moreDetails.architecture: Simple temple architecture near water tanks.

name: Shila Devi Temple
story: Located inside Amber Fort; the idol was brought from Jessore (now Bangladesh) by Raja Man Singh I.

name: Ambikeshwar Mahadev Temple
story: The temple from which the town 'Amer' likely gets its name. The Shiva Linga here is located below floor level and often submerged in water.
highlight: The 22-step descent to the sunken sanctum.
bestTime: Monsoon (when the sanctum fills naturally) or Winter.
entryNotes: Located in the narrow lanes of old Amer town.

moreDetails.history: Built by King Kankil Dev in the 10th century; predates the Amer Fort.
moreDetails.architecture: Older style Rajput architecture; the floor level has risen over centuries.
moreDetails.darshan: Devotees must look down into the pit to see the Linga.
moreDetails.seasonal: In monsoon, the Linga is often fully underwater.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: A hidden gem often missed by tourists visiting Amer Fort.
moreDetails.festivals: Shivratri is celebrated with local fervor.

name: Gautameshwar Mahadev Temple
story: A significant pilgrimage site often called the 'Haridwar of Wagad', located in a scenic valley.
highlight: Ancient Shiva temple with a sacred kund (pond).
entryNotes: Expect a walk down to the valley temple area.

moreDetails.history: Legend links this site to sageautama; it serves as a major redemption spot for tribals.
moreDetails.architecture: Traditional stone temple architecture renovated over time.
moreDetails.darshan: Devotees bathe in the kund before darshan.
moreDetails.seasonal: The landscape is lush green during the monsoon.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: A calm spiritual retreat away from city noise.
moreDetails.festivals: The annual fair in May attracts thousands.

name: Mandaleshwar Temple (Arthuna)
story: The central Shiva shrine in the Arthuna archaeological complex, once the capital of the Paramara rulers of Vagad.
highlight: Exquisite Paramara-era stone carving and complex ruins.
entryNotes: ASI protected site; ticket may be required.

moreDetails.history: Arthuna (Utthunaka) was the 11th-century capital of the Paramaras.
moreDetails.architecture: Features sophisticated Nagara style shikharas and mandapas.
moreDetails.darshan: Many shrines are ruins; the main Mandaleshwar is the highlight.
moreDetails.seasonal: Winters are pleasant for exploring the large site.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: A must-visit for history and archaeology buffs.

name: Avri Mata Temple
story: Renowned for its miraculous healing powers, especially for paralysis and chronic ailments.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: Many devotees stay days for cure.

name: Gadgach Temple
story: A famous 10th-century temple ruin known for having no mortar. It is a 'heap' (Gadgach) of architectural splendor.
highlight: The sheer scale of the ruins and intricate sculpture.

moreDetails.history: Built in the 10th century; destroyed by invaders/time.
moreDetails.architecture: Nagara style; interesting for having no binding material.

name: Kameshwar Mahadev (Auwa)
story: A temple with deep historical ties to the 1857 Indian Rebellion. The revolutionary thakurs of Auwa worshipped here.
highlight: Its association with the 1857 freedom struggle.

moreDetails.history: The center of the rebellion led by Thakur Kushal Singh against the British.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Visit the nearby Sugali Mata temple statue (replica).

name: Kushal Mata Temple
story: Built by Rana Kumbha to commemorate his victory over Malwa; located in the Badnor Fort.

name: Khed Devi Temple
story: Located in the ancient capital of Khed; close to the Ranchhod Rai temple.

name: Ghotia Amba Temple
story: A sacred tribal site where the Pandavas are believed to have stayed; famous for the mango trees (Amba) planted by them.

name: Madareshwar Shiva Temple
story: A cave temple situated inside a high hill, offering a panoramic view of Banswara city.
highlight: Natural cave formation and city views.

moreDetails.history: An ancient natural cave shrine adapted for worship.
moreDetails.seasonal: Greenery surrounds the hill in monsoon.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: The view of Banswara is the second highlight.
moreDetails.festivals: A huge procession (Kavadyatra) starts from here during Shravan.

name: Kakuni Temple Complex
story: A group of ruined temples on the banks of the Parvan river, showcasing the glory of the Pratihara and Paramara eras.
highlight: Scenic riverside location with many ancient temple remains.
bestTime: Winter; monsoon is scenic but access can be muddy.

moreDetails.history: Built between the 8th and 11th centuries; many sculptures are now in Kota/Jhalawar museums.

name: Kapileshwar Mahadev Temple
story: A scenic temple located nearby a pond, associated with the sage Kapila Muni.
highlight: The temple fair is a major event in the Thar desert region.

moreDetails.history: Ancient site renovated in modern times.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Check dates for the local cattle fair held here.
moreDetails.festivals: A large fair is held around Kartik Purnima.

name: Koteshwar Mahadev
story: An ancient temple in the Thar desert, known for its ruins and the resilience of faith in the arid land.

moreDetails.history: Part of the Kiradu style temple tradition.

name: Nandni Mata Temple
story: An ancient temple dedicated to Nandni Mata, widely revered in the Vagad region.

name: Baroli Temples Complex
story: A walled complex of early medieval temples at Baroli, noted for Gurjara-Pratihara architecture and Shiva worship.
highlight: Cluster of stone shrines near the Chambal River.
bestTime: October to March for comfortable weather.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: The complex is spread out; wear comfortable footwear.

moreDetails.history: The Baroli Temples Complex is a group of early medieval shrines in Baroli village under ASI protection.
moreDetails.architecture: The temples are built in the Gurjara-Pratihara style with richly carved stonework.
moreDetails.darshan: Several shrines within the complex are dedicated to Shiva.
moreDetails.seasonal: Winter months are best for exploring the open-air complex.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Carry water and plan time for multiple shrines within the enclosure.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri draws local visitors to the Shiva shrines.

name: Ghateshwar Temple (Baroli)
story: The largest shrine in the Baroli complex, dedicated to Shiva and known for its early medieval stone carving.
highlight: Prominent Shiva shrine within the Baroli temple complex.
bestTime: October to March for cooler exploration of the complex.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: The temple lies within the Baroli complex; allow time for the full site.

moreDetails.history: Ghateshwar Temple is a Shiva shrine within the Baroli temple complex, dated to the early medieval period.
moreDetails.architecture: The shrine reflects Gurjara-Pratihara style with a carved shikhara and mandapa.
moreDetails.darshan: Darshan focuses on the Shiva linga in the main sanctum.
moreDetails.seasonal: Winter brings the best conditions for open-air visits.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Combine with nearby shrines in the Baroli complex.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is the main annual festival at the Shiva shrine.

name: Joganiya Mata Temple
story: Situated amidst scenic waterfalls and forests; historically a hideout for bandits who became devotees.

name: Bhadariya Mata Temple
story: Famous for housing one of Asia's largest underground libraries and a massive Gaushala (cow shelter).

moreDetails.visitorNotes: Unique combination of temple and library.

name: Someshwar Temple (Bhangarh)
story: Located within the 'haunted' Bhangarh Fort, this temple is one of the few structures that remain intact and active.
highlight: Beautiful stone carving in a mysterious, abandoned city.
entryNotes: ASI ticket required; entry prohibited after sunset.

moreDetails.history: Built in the 17th century by Madho Singh, before the fort was abandoned.
moreDetails.architecture: Nagara style with a sanctum and mandapa.
moreDetails.darshan: The linga is present, but active worship is minimal.
moreDetails.seasonal: Winter afternoons are perfect for exploring.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Do not stay after sunset; carry water as there are no shops inside.
moreDetails.festivals: No major festivals due to ASI restrictions.

name: Bhanwal Mata Temple
story: A temple where the Goddess is traditionally offered wine (Madira); features ancient inscriptions.

name: Ganga Mata (Bharatpur)
story: A grand temple dedicated to Goddess Ganga situated within the Lohagarh Fort.

name: Kaila Devi (Lohagarh)
story: A prominent Kaila Devi shrine within Bharatpur, often visited by those who cannot go to Karauli.

name: Bhayad Mata
story: A Sati Mata temple revered by the Rajput community in Barmer.

name: Harni Mahadev
story: A popular Shiva temple located on a hill near Bhilwara city, famous for its 3-day annual fair.
highlight: Hilltop location offering views of the city.

moreDetails.history: An old shrine developed into a major tourist spot.
moreDetails.darshan: Climb up the hill for darshan.
moreDetails.festivals: The fair attracts lakhs of people.

name: Triveni Sangam Mahadev
story: Located at the holy confluence of three rivers: Banas, Bedach, and Menali. It is a major site for immersion of ashes and spiritual cleansing.
highlight: The confluence point (Triveni) of three rivers.

moreDetails.history: Ancient pilgrimage site for Mewar region.

name: Khimaj Mata Temple
story: An ancient temple dedicated to Kshemankari (Khimaj) Mata; Kuldevi of the Solanki Rajputs.

name: Hazareshwar Mahadev Temple
story: Part of the Bijolia temple group, famous for a large Shiva Linga covered with hundreds of smaller miniature lingas.

moreDetails.history: Built during the Chahamana era (11th-12th century).
moreDetails.architecture: Bhumija style with high artistic value.
moreDetails.darshan: Close-up view of the unique linga.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Look closely to see the miniature lingas carved on the main one.

name: Undeshwar Mahadev Temple
story: A prominent temple in the Bijolia group where the Shiva Linga is located below the floor level (Undeshwar).
highlight: The sanctum is partly underground; fine Bhumija architecture.
entryNotes: Part of the protected Bijolia temple group.

moreDetails.history: Built during the Chahamana period, reflecting high medieval artistry.
moreDetails.architecture: Bhumija style with a stellar plan and intricate carvings.
moreDetails.darshan: Devotees descend a few steps to view the linga.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Visit the nearby Mandakini Kund as well.
moreDetails.festivals: A major hub for Shivratri in Bhilwara.

name: Shivbari Temple
story: A grand temple built of red sandstone by Maharaja Doongar Singh, featuring a four-faced Shiva linga and fortress-like walls.
highlight: The four-faced black marble Shiva Linga and red sandstone architecture.

moreDetails.history: Built in the late 19th century by Maharaja Doongar Singh to honor his father.
moreDetails.architecture: Rajput style with high fortified walls and intricate jali work.
moreDetails.darshan: Devotees can see the Nandi facing the four-faced Linga.
moreDetails.seasonal: Pleasant in winter; hot in summer.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Photography of the idol may be restricted.

name: Aai Mata Temple
story: The main temple of Aai Mata, worshipped by the Seervi community; famous because the lamp's flame produces saffron instead of soot.

name: Bisaldeo Temple
story: A 12th-century Shiva temple at Bisalpur, known for its riverside setting and partial submersion during high water.
highlight: Stone temple beside the Bisalpur Dam reservoir.
bestTime: Post-monsoon for water views and pleasant weather.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Water levels can affect access to the lower courtyard.

moreDetails.history: Bisaldeo is a 12th-century Shiva temple commissioned in the Chahamana period near the Banas River.
moreDetails.architecture: The temple includes a garbhagriha, mandapa, and stone shikhara typical of the era.
moreDetails.darshan: Darshan is offered at the Shiva linga in the main sanctum.
moreDetails.seasonal: Reservoir levels can partially submerge the courtyard during heavy rains.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Plan visits in daylight and check access during monsoon months.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is the main annual observance.

name: Gokarneshwar Mahadev Temple
story: An ancient temple built by Vigraharaja IV, located scenically near the massive Bisalpur Dam.
highlight: Proximity to the Bisalpur Dam reservoir.
bestTime: Monsoon (to see the dam) and Winter.
entryNotes: Popular picnic spot due to the dam.

moreDetails.history: Commissioned by the Chauhan king Vigraharaja IV (Bisal Deo) in the 12th century.
moreDetails.architecture: Features a large Mandapa and sanctum; partially submerged during high floods in the past.
moreDetails.darshan: A spiritual stop during a dam visit.
moreDetails.seasonal: The reservoir is full after monsoon.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Combine with a trip to the Bisalpur Dam.

name: Bhimlat Mahadev Temple
story: A Shiva temple near the Bhimlat waterfall, visited for both pilgrimage and scenic landscapes.
highlight: Waterfall backdrop and forested Aravalli setting.
bestTime: Monsoon and early winter for waterfall flow.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Monsoon paths can be slippery; use caution near the falls.

moreDetails.history: Bhimlat Mahadev Temple is a Shiva shrine near Bhimlat Waterfall in Bundi district.
moreDetails.architecture: The temple is a modest hill shrine adjacent to the waterfall area.
moreDetails.darshan: Darshan is offered at the Shiva shrine with the falls nearby.
moreDetails.seasonal: Monsoon months bring the strongest waterfall flow.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Plan for a mixed pilgrimage and nature visit.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is a key local observance.

name: Sheetla Mata (Chaksu)
story: The main seat of Sheetla Mata in Rajasthan; famous for the 'Basoda' festival where stale food is offered.

name: Chauth Mata Temple
story: One of the most significant temples for married women; the primary deity of the Karwa Chauth festival.

name: Annapurna Mata (Chittorgarh)
story: Another significant temple within the fort complex; Annapurna is the provider of food.

name: Kalika Mata (Chittorgarh)
story: Originally a Sun Temple from the 8th century, converted to a Kalika temple; a symbol of the fort's resilience.

name: Kukadeshwar Mahadev
story: Located near the Bassi fort, this site features ancient temple ruins and a seasonal waterfall.
highlight: The 11th-century ruins and the scenic waterfall.

name: Samadhishvara Temple
story: An 11th-century Shiva temple inside Chittor Fort, known for its long restoration history.
highlight: Fort-side Shiva shrine with layered sculptural styles.
bestTime: Winter months for fort exploration and temple visits.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Located within Chittor Fort; ticketing follows fort entry rules.

moreDetails.history: Samadhishvara Temple is a Shiva shrine within Chittor Fort, with origins dated to the 11th century and later restorations.
moreDetails.architecture: The temple includes a sanctum, antarala, and mandapa with carved stone detailing.
moreDetails.darshan: Darshan focuses on the Shiva deity known as Samadhishvara.
moreDetails.seasonal: Winter is best for exploring the fort precincts.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Combine with nearby fort monuments during the same visit.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is the main annual festival for the shrine.

name: Shiva Temple (Chittorgarh Fort)
story: A Shiva shrine within the sprawling Chittorgarh Fort precincts, part of the fort's temple landscape.
highlight: Fort-side Shiva shrine amid Chittorgarh's historic monuments.
bestTime: Winter months for long walks across the fort.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season and fort access hours.
entryNotes: Entry follows Chittorgarh Fort access rules and ticketing.

moreDetails.history: Chittorgarh Fort is one of the largest forts in India and contains numerous temples within its precincts.
moreDetails.architecture: The Shiva shrine is part of the fort's stone-built temple landscape.
moreDetails.darshan: Darshan takes place at the Shiva shrine within the fort complex.
moreDetails.seasonal: Winter offers the most comfortable conditions for fort visits.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Plan for significant walking between fort monuments and temples.

name: Tulja Bhavani (Chittorgarh)
story: Built by Banvir; dedicated to Tulja Bhavani, the Kuldevi of Chhatrapati Shivaji.

name: Suiya Mahadev
story: Known for the 'Suiya Mela', which occurs only on specific astrological conjunctions, making it the 'Kumbh of the Desert'.
highlight: The rare fair that happens every few years.
entryNotes: Located near the Pakistan border area.

moreDetails.history: Ancient site revered by desert communities.
moreDetails.darshan: Deeply religious atmosphere during the fair.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Check fair dates before planning for the festival.
moreDetails.festivals: Suiya Mela is a massive event.

name: Mansa Devi (Churu)
story: Dedicated to Manasa Devi, the goddess of snakes; features distinct Shekhawati frescoes.

name: Dant Mata Temple
story: Named after the 'teeth' of the goddess; a regional protector deity.

name: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple (Dausa)
story: A hilltop Shiva temple on Devgiri Hill, reached by a long staircase and known for its local pilgrimage traditions.
highlight: Devgiri hill ascent and panoramic views around Dausa.
bestTime: Early mornings or cooler winter days for the climb.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Expect a stair climb; carry water and visit during daylight hours.

moreDetails.history: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple sits on Devgiri Hill in Dausa district and is a key local Shiva pilgrimage.
moreDetails.architecture: The temple complex crowns the hilltop, with a prominent approach via steps.
moreDetails.darshan: Darshan focuses on the Shiva shrine at the hill summit.
moreDetails.seasonal: Shravan and Mahashivratri bring the highest footfall.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: The climb can be steep; plan early to avoid heat.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri and Shravan month are peak devotional periods.

name: Kunjal Mata Temple
story: The Kuldevi of the Pareek Brahmin community; a beautiful white marble temple.

name: Karni Mata Temple
story: The famous Temple of Rats; Karni Mata is believed to be an incarnation of Durga. The holy rats (kabas) are considered her children.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: Spotting a white rat is lucky.

name: Parshuram Mahadev Temple
story: A cave Shiva temple in the Aravalli hills, approached by a long stairway and mountain path.
highlight: Cave shrine with a scenic hill approach.
bestTime: Winter mornings and post-monsoon months for trekking comfort.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Expect a long staircase and hill walk; carry water.

moreDetails.history: Parshuram Mahadev Temple is a Shiva cave shrine located on the border of Pali and Rajsamand districts.
moreDetails.architecture: The sanctum is inside a rock-cut cave with a stairway approach.
moreDetails.darshan: Darshan takes place within the cave shrine.
moreDetails.seasonal: Monsoon greenery is beautiful, but winter is easiest for the climb.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Plan for a longer visit due to the hill ascent.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri and Shravan attract large pilgrim gatherings.

name: Dhanop Mata Temple
story: An ancient temple built by Raja Dhana; the idol is smeared with sindoor (vermilion).

name: Chopadeshwar Mahadev
story: A mysterious temple located amidst the rocky ravines of the Chambal region.
highlight: The rugged landscape of Dholpur's ravines.
entryNotes: Remote location; go with a guide.

name: Machkund Temple
story: A sacred tank surrounded by 108 temples. It is called the 'Nephew of Pilgrimages' (Teerthon Ka Bhanja).
highlight: The scenic tank surrounded by ancient red sandstone temples.

moreDetails.history: Named after King Muchukund; legendary site mentioned in Puranas.
moreDetails.architecture: Series of chhatris and temples in red sandstone.

name: Bhuvaneshwar Mahadev
story: A revered temple featuring a swayambhu (self-manifested) Shiva Linga and natural caves nearby.
highlight: The Rangpanchami fair held here is very famous.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: Witness the Gair dance during the fair.

name: Deo Somnath Temple
story: A spectacular 12th-century temple built of white stone without using any lime or cement, standing on 148 pillars.
bestTime: Winter months; monsoon offers river views.
entryNotes: Located 24km from Dungarpur; local transport available.

moreDetails.history: Built in the 12th century, it is a masterpiece of Sompura architecture.
moreDetails.architecture: Three-story structure built with interlocking stones.
moreDetails.darshan: The shivling is located deep within the sanctum.
moreDetails.seasonal: The Som river flows full during the monsoon.

name: Madareshwar Temple
story: A cave temple located inside a hill; dedicated to Shiva and Shakti.

name: Vijay Rajrajeshwar Temple
story: A stunning temple situated on the banks of the Gaib Sagar Lake, built by Maharawal Vijay Singh. It is dedicated to Shiva and boasts intricate carving.
highlight: The location on the lake edge and the craftsmanship.
entryNotes: Located near the Udai Bilas Palace.

moreDetails.history: Commissioned by Maharawal Vijay Singh in the late 19th century.
moreDetails.architecture: Mix of Rajput and Mughal styles.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Visit the Badal Mahal inside the lake as well.

name: Hinglaj Mata (Fatehgarh)
story: A prominent temple of Hinglaj Mata in the Thar desert, serving devotees who cannot visit the main shrine in Pakistan.

name: Ghantiyali Mata
story: Located near Tanot; believed to be the sister of Tanot Mata. Validates the protection of the border.

name: Dadhimati Mata Temple
story: One of the oldest surviving temples (4th century Gupta era); Kuldevi of the Dadhich Brahmins.

name: Bhadra Kali Temple
story: Located on the banks of the Ghaggar river; Emperor Akbar is said to have visited and offered a red canopy.

name: Harshnath Temple
story: An ancient Shiva temple on Harsh hill in Sikar, known for its ruins and hilltop setting.
highlight: Hilltop ruins with carved pillars and regional views.
bestTime: Winter and early spring for clear hilltop weather.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Expect a hill drive and short walk to the site.

moreDetails.history: Harshnath is an ancient Shiva temple in Sikar district associated with early medieval inscriptions.
moreDetails.architecture: The temple and surrounding shrines are largely in ruins but retain carved stone elements.
moreDetails.darshan: Darshan is offered at the remaining Shiva shrine on the hill.
moreDetails.seasonal: Winter brings the best visibility and comfort at the hilltop.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Carry water and plan for wind exposure on the hill.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is the main annual observance.

name: Bijasan Mata (Indergarh)
story: A major Shakti Peeth in the Hadoti region; located on a high hill requiring a climb of 750 steps.

name: Kamleshwar Mahadev
story: A prominent temple in Indergarh, associated with the Hada rulers. It is a major center for local faith.
highlight: The nearby stepwells and fort walls.

moreDetails.visitorNotes: Visit the Bijasan Mata temple nearby.

name: Ambika Mata (Jagat)
story: Known as the 'Khajuraho of Mewar' for its exquisite sculptures; an ancient temple from the 10th century.

name: Bhooteshwar Mahadev Temple
story: A small temple nestled in the Aravalli hills behind Nahargarh Fort, popular among trekkers.
highlight: The trek through the forest to reach the temple.
entryNotes: Accessible via a trek from Sagar Lake (Amer).

moreDetails.history: An old shrine used by ascetics in the hills.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Do not go alone; leopards are known to be in the area.

name: Jharkhand Mahadev Temple
story: A prominent modern temple in Jaipur known for its South Indian architectural style and massive devotee base.
highlight: South Indian style Gopuram (tower) in North India.
entryNotes: Located in the city; easy access but parking can be tight.

moreDetails.history: Constructed in the early 20th century, but gained major prominence recently.
moreDetails.darshan: Lines are segregated for men and women.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Strict dress code is often enforced (no shorts).
moreDetails.festivals: The temple is decorated grandly for Janmashtami and Shivratri.

name: Tarkeshwar Nath Temple
story: A historic Shiva temple in Jaipur's old city, known locally as Tadkeshwar Mahadev.
highlight: Old-city Shiva shrine with traditional Jaipur ambience.
bestTime: Morning darshan in the old city; winter months for pleasant walks.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Expect city traffic; plan parking or use local transport.

moreDetails.history: Tarkeshwar Nath Temple is a Shiva shrine in Jaipur, also known as Tadkeshwar Mahadev.
moreDetails.architecture: The temple reflects traditional Jaipur-era shrine architecture.
moreDetails.darshan: Darshan centers on the Shiva linga within the main sanctum.
moreDetails.seasonal: Shravan and Mahashivratri are the most crowded periods.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Visit early to avoid old-city congestion.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri and Shravan Mondays draw large crowds.

name: Raj Rajeshwar Temple
story: A serene Shiva temple located inside the Golden Fort, showcasing the intricate stone carving skills of Jaisalmer's artisans.
highlight: Yellow sandstone architecture inside a living fort.
entryNotes: Located inside the fort; no extra ticket for the temple.

moreDetails.history: Built by the Bhati rulers for their personal worship.
moreDetails.architecture: Intricate Jali (lattice) work in yellow sandstone.
moreDetails.darshan: A quiet spot amidst the tourist hustle of the fort.
moreDetails.seasonal: Perfect escape from the winter sun.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is celebrated by the locals living in the fort.

name: Sangeeshwar Mahadev Temple
story: Located in the ancient capital of Lodurva, this temple stands amidst ruins of a once-great city.
highlight: Proximity to the famous Jain temples of Lodurva.

moreDetails.history: Lodurva was the Bhati capital before Jaisalmer.
moreDetails.architecture: Ornate carvings typical of the region.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Combine with a visit to the Lodurva Jain Temple.

name: Temde Rai Mata
story: Another form of Hinglaj Mata worshipped in the deep desert; known for miracles.

name: Sire Mandir
story: Located at the very top of the formidable Jalore Fort, this temple is dedicated to the Nath yogi Jallinath.
highlight: The strenuous climb and the commanding view from the summit.
entryNotes: Requires a steep hike up the fort.

moreDetails.history: Built by Rawal Ratan Singh in honor of the Nath saint.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Carry water; the climb is tough.
moreDetails.festivals: Local devotees climb in large numbers on Shivratri.

name: Jamwai Mata Temple
story: The Kuldevi of the Kachwaha clan (Jaipur royals); located near the Ramgarh lake.

name: Bhatiyani Mata (Majisa)
story: A princess turned deity, affectionately called Majisa; worshipped for prosperity and family well-being.

name: Khandia Mahadev
story: An ancient Shiva temple located just outside Jhalawar, known for its old architectural style.
highlight: The antiquity of the site and peace.

moreDetails.history: Part of the rich temple heritage of Hadoti.

name: Pataleshwar Mahadev
story: Located in Jhalrapatan (City of Bells), this temple is distinct from the famous Sun Temple and Sitaleshwar. The sanctum is below ground level.

moreDetails.history: Built during the height of Jhalrapatan's temple building era.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Jhalrapatan is a temple town; walk around to see many others.

name: Sitaleshwar Mahadev Temple
story: Considered one of the oldest dated temples in Rajasthan (689 AD), famous for its elegant pillars.
highlight: Early Gupta-style architecture and proximity to the Chandrabhaga river.
entryNotes: Located within the Chandrabhaga temple complex.

moreDetails.history: Dated to 689 AD, making it a key monument in Indian temple history.
moreDetails.architecture: Features a flat-roofed sabhamandapa and exquisite carving.
moreDetails.darshan: The sanctum contains a Shiva linga.
moreDetails.seasonal: The Kartik fair (Nov) brings a vibrant cattle fair to the riverbanks.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Visit the nearby Sun Temple in Jhalrapatan as well.
moreDetails.festivals: Kartik Purnima is the main event.

name: Rani Sati Dadi Temple
story: A massive temple complex dedicated to Dadiji; a symbol of matriarchal power and prosperity for the Marwari community.

name: Jwala Mata Temple
story: A very old Shakti Peeth of the Khangarot Kachwaha clan; located on a hillock in Jobner.

name: Achalnath Mahadev Temple
story: A historic temple in the heart of Jodhpur's old city, commissioned by Rao Ganga in the 16th century.
highlight: Traditional architecture in the bustling old bazaar.
bestTime: Early morning or evening for Aarti.
entryNotes: Located in a busy market area; parking is difficult.

moreDetails.history: Constructed by Nanak Devi, queen of Rao Ganga, in 1531.
moreDetails.architecture: Made of Chhitar stone with carved mandapa halls.
moreDetails.darshan: Main sanctum houses the Shiva linga.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Experience the old city vibe of Jodhpur here.

name: Barke Devi
story: A lesser-known cave temple in the rocky terrain around Jodhpur.

name: Chamunda Mata (Mehrangarh)
story: The royal deity of Jodhpur, located at the southern end of the majestic Mehrangarh Fort.

name: Maha Mandir
story: A massive architectural marvel built in 1812 by Maharaja Man Singh. It serves as the headquarters of the Nath sect and stands on 84 beautifully carved pillars.
highlight: The 84 intricate pillars and its significance as a Nath yoga center.
entryNotes: Located within Jodhpur city; easily accessible.

moreDetails.history: Built by Maharaja Man Singh who was a devout follower of the Nath yogis.
moreDetails.architecture: Unique walled town style with 84 pillars supporting the main shrine.
moreDetails.darshan: Focus is on the yoga posture carvings.
moreDetails.festivals: Guru Purnima is celebrated with great pomp.

name: Nagnechi Mata Temple
story: The Kuldevi of the Rathore clan; originally brought from Karnataka. The idol is traditionally made of Neem wood.

name: Siddhnath Mahadev Temple
story: A remote temple located in the rocky hills near Kaylana Lake, accessible by a raw stone staircase cut into the mountain.
highlight: rugged trekking path and isolation from the city.
timings: Open daily; best visited in daylight.
entryNotes: Requires a steep climb/walk; not for those with mobility issues.

moreDetails.history: Built by a hermit (saint) named Veetrag Narain Swami.
moreDetails.architecture: Simple structure, but the location is majestic.
moreDetails.darshan: Peaceful darshan away from city crowds.
moreDetails.seasonal: The hills turn green during the monsoon.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Carry water; the path is rocky.

name: Kaila Devi Temple
story: A major pilgrimage site on the banks of Kali Sil river; dedicated to Kaila Devi (Mahalakshmi/Chamunda).

name: Eklingji Temple
story: A historic Shiva temple complex near Kailashpuri that anchors the sacred landscape around Nagda in the Udaipur region.
highlight: Stone temple complex associated with the Mewar tradition of Shiva worship.
bestTime: Early morning for quieter darshan; winter months are comfortable.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Plan for temple protocols and queues during major festivals.

moreDetails.history: Eklingji is a Shiva temple complex in Kailashpuri village of Udaipur district, historically tied to the Mewar tradition.
moreDetails.architecture: The complex includes multiple shrines and stone temple structures typical of regional styles.
moreDetails.darshan: Darshan centers on the main Shiva shrine within the complex.
moreDetails.seasonal: Winter and early spring are the most pleasant months for visits.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Combine visits with nearby heritage sites around Nagda.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is the most prominent annual observance.

name: Kameshwar Mahadev (Kaman)
story: Situated in Kaman (Kamyavan), part of the Braj region. The Chaurasi Khamba temple here is an ancient masterpiece.
entryNotes: Part of the Chaurasi Kos Parikrama.

moreDetails.history: Ancient site believed to be from the Dwapar Yuga; renovated by various rulers.
moreDetails.architecture: Reuse of ancient pillars in a mosque/temple hybrid structure.
moreDetails.festivals: Braj Yatra pilgrims visit in large numbers.

name: Kanswa Shiva Temple
story: A Shiva shrine in Kanswa village of Kota district, known for its archaeological setting.
highlight: Village Shiva temple tied to Kanswa's archaeological history.
bestTime: October to March for pleasant weather in Hadoti.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: The temple is within a village setting; respect local customs.

moreDetails.history: Kanswa is a village in Kota district known for archaeological importance and a local Shiva shrine.
moreDetails.architecture: The temple is a compact stone shrine within the village precincts.
moreDetails.darshan: Darshan focuses on the Shiva linga in the main sanctum.
moreDetails.seasonal: Winter is most comfortable for village visits.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Plan a short stop; facilities are limited.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is the primary local celebration.

name: Sitabari (Sita Temple)
story: Believed to be the place where Goddess Sita lived during her exile and where Luv-Kush were born.

name: Sitabari Temples
story: A scenic spot with natural springs (kunds) where Sita is believed to have stayed. It features shrines to Shiva, Laxman, and Valmiki.
highlight: The natural water tanks (Kunds) and the massive annual fair.
entryNotes: The site of the 'Kumbh of the Sahariyas'.

moreDetails.architecture: Group of small temples around water tanks.
moreDetails.darshan: Bathing in the kunds is the primary ritual.
moreDetails.seasonal: The fair in summer is dusty but vibrant.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Key cultural center for the Sahariya tribe.

name: Rameshwaram Mahadev Temple
story: Situated at the confluence of the Banas and Chambal rivers, this is a scenic pilgrimage spot often called the 'Prayag of Rajasthan'.
highlight: The confluence (Sangam) of two major rivers.
bestTime: Winter; monsoon travel can be tricky.
entryNotes: Located near the Ranthambore sanctuary boundaries.

moreDetails.history: An ancient site associated with Parashurama.
moreDetails.darshan: Devotees bathe in the river before worship.
moreDetails.seasonal: River levels rise significantly in monsoon.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Wildlife from Ranthambore is sometimes sighted nearby.

name: Keway Mata Temple
story: A 10th-century temple built by the Chahamanas; famous for its historical inscription.

name: Kiradu Temples
story: A group of ruined temples in the desert landscape of Barmer, with the Someshvara Shiva temple best preserved.
highlight: Carved columns and Maru-Gurjara stonework among the ruins.
bestTime: Winter months for desert travel comfort.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: The site is remote; plan transport and daylight visits.

moreDetails.history: Kiradu is a group of temple ruins in Barmer district with multiple Shiva shrines, including the Someshvara temple.
moreDetails.architecture: The remains show Maru-Gurjara style stone carving and richly decorated pillars.
moreDetails.darshan: Visitors focus on surviving sanctums and sculpted mandapas.
moreDetails.seasonal: Post-monsoon and winter weather is best for desert excursions.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Carry water and sun protection; facilities are limited.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is observed by local devotees.

name: Sati Mata (Kishangarh)
story: A historical Sati temple in the city famous for its marble and Bani Thani paintings.

name: Char Choma Mahadev Temple
story: A hidden archaeological treasure, this is one of the few surviving temples from the Gupta period in Rajasthan.
highlight: Rare Gupta-era architecture and flat-roofed style.
entryNotes: Located about 30km from Kota; requires private transport.

moreDetails.history: Dates back to the Gupta empire (approx 5th-6th century AD).
moreDetails.architecture: Flat roof (unlike the later shikhara style) with heavy stone pillars.
moreDetails.darshan: A step back in time to ancient India.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: A must for history students and archaeology enthusiasts.

name: Garadia Mahadev Temple
story: A Shiva temple perched on a cliff edge offering a breathtaking view of the Chambal River's horseshoe bend.
highlight: Panoramic view of the Chambal river canyon.
bestTime: Monsoon and winter for lush greenery and clear views.
timings: Open daily; entry usually closes before sunset.
entryNotes: Requires a ticket for vehicle entry; located within a forest zone.

moreDetails.history: A local shrine that gained fame for its dramatic location overlooking the Chambal gorge.
moreDetails.architecture: Simple shrine structure; the natural setting is the main attraction.
moreDetails.darshan: The shrine is small, but the view of the river gorge is the spiritual highlight.
moreDetails.seasonal: Monsoon brings waterfalls and green landscapes.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Careful near the cliff edges; carry water and snacks.

name: Geparnath Mahadev Temple
story: A Shiva temple situated deep in a gorge near Kota, accessible by a long flight of stairs.
highlight: Natural waterfall dropping directly onto the temple area.
entryNotes: Requires descending ~300 steps; difficult for elderly.

moreDetails.history: An ancient spot dating back to the 16th century, associated with royal patronage.
moreDetails.architecture: Cave-like shrine integrated into the rock face.
moreDetails.darshan: The Shiva linga is often bathed by the natural spring water.
moreDetails.seasonal: Access can be closed during heavy rains due to flash floods.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Monkeys are common; keep food hidden.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri sees heavy footfall despite the steep climb.

name: Karneshwar Temple
story: A historic Shiva temple in Kota that serves as a popular spiritual getaway for city dwellers.
highlight: The peaceful complex and old architecture.

moreDetails.history: Built by the rulers of Kota.

name: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple (Kumbhalgarh Fort)
story: A Shiva shrine within Kumbhalgarh Fort, one of the major Mewar hill forts of Rajasthan.
highlight: Temple visit combined with the ramparts and views of Kumbhalgarh Fort.
bestTime: Winter months for fort walks and temple visits.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season and fort access hours.
entryNotes: Temple access follows Kumbhalgarh Fort entry rules.

moreDetails.history: Kumbhalgarh Fort is a major Mewar hill fort in Rajsamand district, with multiple Hindu temples inside its walls.
moreDetails.architecture: The temple follows regional fort-temple architecture within the Kumbhalgarh complex.
moreDetails.darshan: Darshan takes place at the Shiva shrine inside the fort precincts.
moreDetails.seasonal: Winter provides the best weather for fort exploration.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Allocate time for both the temple and fort ramparts.
moreDetails.festivals: Mahashivratri is the key devotional day.

name: Paplaj Mata Temple
story: Situated in the hills of Lalsot; a serene temple requiring a short trek.

name: Phool Bai Mata
story: The Samadhi temple of Phool Bai, a female saint revered as a goddess.

name: Karni Mata (Mathania)
story: An important temple of Karni Mata in the town famous for its red chilies.

name: Menal Temple Complex (Mahanal)
story: A historic Saiva temple complex at Menal, noted for Bhumija architecture and its role as a Shaiva center.
highlight: Bhumija-style Shiva temple with carved exterior panels.
bestTime: October to March for comfortable weather.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: The site is open-air; plan for sun and limited facilities.

moreDetails.history: The Mahanal temple at Menal was a major center of Saivism under the Chahamanas, with an 11th-century Shiva temple.
moreDetails.architecture: The main temple is Bhumija style with a pancharatha plan, shikhara, and a separate Nandi mandapa.
moreDetails.darshan: Darshan focuses on the Shiva shrine within the main temple.
moreDetails.seasonal: Post-monsoon and winter are best for exploring the complex.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: The complex includes multiple shrines and a matha; allow time to walk the site.

name: Mahodara Mata
story: Mahodara (Big Bellied) Mata; local legend says trains used to stop here automatically if not halted.

name: Suswani Mata Temple
story: Kuldevi of the Surana, Dugar, and Sankhla clans; the Goddess merged into a Ker tree to save herself.

name: Achaleshwar Mahadev Temple
story: A historic temple outside Achalgarh Fort where Shiva is worshipped in the form of a toe, centered around a natural Nandi statue.
highlight: Worship of Shiva's toe and the brass Nandi statue.
bestTime: All year round; monsoon and winter are especially scenic.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Located near the fort parking; minimal walking required.

moreDetails.history: Built in the 9th century by the Paramara dynasty and later renovated by Maharana Kumbha.
moreDetails.architecture: Features a mandapa and sanctum with ancient sculpted pillars.
moreDetails.darshan: Devotees view the 'Brahma Khadd' where the toe is enshrined.
moreDetails.seasonal: Monsoon clouds often cover the fort area.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Visit Achalgarh Fort nearby for panoramic views.

name: Arbuda Devi (Adhar Devi)
story: A cave temple located high up in Mount Abu; the 'Adhar' (lips) of the Goddess are worshipped here.

name: Ashapura Mata (Nadol)
story: The ancient capital of the Chauhans and the primary seat of Ashapura Mata, the fulfiller of wishes (Asha).

name: Baal Mata Temple
story: Worshipped as the protector of children (Baal form).

name: Rupal Mata
story: Worshipped by the local Bhil and Rajput communities; famous for the 'Palki' procession.

name: Ganeshwar Mahadev
story: An archaeological site known for the Ganeshwar-Jodhpura culture. The Shiva temple here has a natural hot sulfur spring.
highlight: Hot springs and the ancient archaeological mounds nearby.

moreDetails.history: Ganeshwar is a 4000-year-old civilization site; the temple is the modern spiritual center.
moreDetails.seasonal: Winters are cold but good for hot springs.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Archaeology lovers should visit the mounds.

name: Markand Devi Temple
story: Dedicated to the mother Goddess as worshipped by Sage Markandeya.

name: Harihara Temples (Osian)
story: A group of temples dedicated to Harihara (the union of Shiva and Vishnu), representing the zenith of Pratihara architecture.
highlight: The syncretic deity (Half Shiva, Half Vishnu) and exquisite carvings.
entryNotes: Part of the Osian temple cluster.

moreDetails.history: Built in the 8th-9th centuries by the Gurjara-Pratiharas.
moreDetails.architecture: Panchayatana style (main shrine surrounded by 4 subsidiary shrines).
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Do not miss the Sun Temple nearby.
moreDetails.festivals: No active worship in the ruins.

name: Sacchiyay Mata Temple
story: An 8th-century temple dedicated to Sacchiyay Mata (Sachiya); Kuldevi of the Oswal Jains and Rajputs.

name: Nimbo Ka Nath Mahadev Temple
story: Legend says Kunti (mother of Pandavas) worshipped Shiva here during their exile. The temple is known for its large annual fairs.
entryNotes: Located on the main road; easy access.

moreDetails.history: Ancient site renovated over time; strong local folklore connection.
moreDetails.darshan: Very popular with the Rebari and local communities.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Good stopover when traveling between Jodhpur and Udaipur.
moreDetails.festivals: The fairs attract thousands of rural devotees.

name: Pallu Wali Mata (Brahmani)
story: Built on the ruins of an old Kalibangan-era site; the idol is finely carved and very revered in the north.

name: Latiyal Mata Temple
story: Also known as Khejri Beri Rai; the throne of the goddess is surrounded by Khejri trees.

name: Pipaad Mata
story: An ancient Shakti shrine in the Pipaad city; revered by the local trading communities.

name: Amba Mata (Pratapgarh)
story: The main Shakti temple of Pratapgarh; central to the local tribal and Rajput culture.

name: Aptaheshwar Temple
story: One of the most important Shiva temples in Pushkar, built in the 12th century. It was destroyed by Aurangzeb and later rebuilt.
highlight: Historical significance in the holy town of Pushkar.

moreDetails.history: Ancient origins; current structure is from the 18th century.
moreDetails.darshan: Part of the Pushkar pilgrimage circuit.

name: Atmateshwar Mahadev Temple
